**V4.50 fold-in record (July 2, 2026):** Prior-art closure, no new computation, no version-content conflict with V4.49 — the tetrahedral symmetry cap **G-2a-S2** found on the canonical golden-ellipse Borromean representative is shown to generalize to **every planar-per-strand symmetric Borromean embedding**, via a peer-reviewed classification theorem. Arc shape is unconstrained by the theorem — straight, circular, elliptical, or arbitrarily elaborate; the only condition is |I| ≠ |T|. **This is the exact general form of what G-2a-S2 found for the golden-ellipse family (a=φ, b=1/φ, i.e. a≠b):** the ellipse computation tested one point in this classification; the theorem covers the entire family, any strand shape, in one closed statement, independently derived and published with no relation to this project. **Why this closes the "richer embedding" question (planar-strand case).** Canon's own May 12, 2026 methodological note ("The Metric Shape Is Not The Object", filed in the session-close record) holds that a symmetry claim about one specific Császár/Szilassi coordinate embedding is not ledger-worthy, since the polyhedron has multiple valid, non-isometric realizations (Bokowski–Eggert 1991); picking a second embedding and re-testing its point group would repeat exactly that error. The classification theorem sidesteps this cleanly — it is a statement about every strand shape in the symmetric-Borromean family at once, satisfying the embedding-independence the note requires. **Scope of closure.** A K₇-tube/Szilassi core built from three strands confined to the three coordinate planes with the standard 3-fold-rotation-plus-reflection symmetry — canon's own established picture (§2.15's three colored strands; the same symmetry type G-2a-S2 computed directly for the ellipse family) — falls inside this classification regardless of how elaborate the individual strand shape gets from the K₇/Szilassi combinatorics. No such core can be octahedral while remaining genuinely (non-degenerately) Borromean. **Residual, honestly flagged, not closed.** The classification covers planar-per-strand configurations only. A genuinely non-planar-per-strand core — each strand winding through all three spatial dimensions rather than sitting in a single coordinate plane — falls outside the theorem and is not addressed by it: a real, narrower gap, and also not a structure canon currently describes anywhere. **Net disposition.** The standing open question from V4.49 ("can the K₇-tube/Szilassi core be simultaneously octahedral and genuinely Borromean?") is answered **NO for the planar-per-strand case, by a general theorem**, not merely "found tetrahedral for one representative." §2.87.A's octahedral premise remains a **located import** (as V4.49 filed it), now with the location sharpened: no planar-per-strand core, however elaborate, will supply it; any recovery would have to come from a non-planar-per-strand structure canon has not built. ## Preamble

### The Prior Address Standard

A derivation is structural when every constant and integer in it can be derived from the framework's axioms before consulting the experimental target. A constant selected because it is near the right answer is a parameter, not a derivation.

For any new constant or integer introduced into the framework:

1. What mathematical object defines this constant?
2. Where does that object appear in the framework's axioms, independently of the physical target?
3. Can you write down the constant's value without knowing the experimental result?

If the answer to question 3 is no, the constant is a parameter; it is labeled as a conjecture until a prior address is established.

### The Eddington Maneuver

Computing a residual, identifying a correction factor that closes it, and asserting the correction factor is "explained by" a geometric structure without deriving the correction factor's value from that structure independently. This failure mode has been identified and retracted multiple times across all sessions. Any future instance must be caught and logged immediately.

### Vocabulary Substitution

Physics-adjacent terminology without axiomatic derivation does not constitute a prior address. Retired terms include: impedance, flux density, topological friction, topological silt, cavitation, Red Tiles, bunching of the rug, gauge equilibrium (in data science contexts), topological strain (in data science contexts). *(Forward pointer, V4.20: the mechanism behind this clause is **M.CW (The Category Wall)** below — physics-adjacent vocabulary fails as a prior address precisely because the dimensionful quantity it names cannot come from the combinatorial object the construction contains.)*

### Register System

- **Register 1 (R1):** Formal derivation from axioms; numerical/symbolic verification complete.
- **Register 2 (R2):** Motivated proof sketch or structural observation with R1 derivation targets named.
- **Register 3 (R3):** Narrative or pedagogical framing; not citable as result.

Registers must not collapse into one another. Two working modes exist: **Exploration** (conjecture-labeled, free) and **Audit** (full Prior Address Standard, append-only).

### The Category Wall (M.CW)

*(Methodological note, June 1, 2026. R1 as a no-go constraint. Surfaced in the Phase-B meson audit; banked decoupled from the falsified physical claim. Parallel in kind to M.2π / M.SE.)*

**Statement.** Purely combinatorial input — incidence/adjacency data, a finite group's multiplication table, the bare graph or design underlying a construction — cannot, by itself, produce (1) a **dimensionful constant**, (2) a **metric** (distance, angle, signature), or (3) a **sign** (orientation, chirality, sign of a coupling). Dynamics needs all three. Combinatorics alone fixes only **dimensionless ratios** and the **algebraic form** of an interaction. To obtain a scale, a metric, or a sign, additional structure must be *posited*, and that posited structure is an import subject to the Prior Address Standard, not an output of the combinatorial object. It is a constraint-stating result, not a derivation: it says what a combinatorial construction cannot output.

**Why (invariance argument).** Pure combinatorial data is invariant under global rescaling (no distinguished unit), reflection/relabeling (unoriented incidence carries no handedness), and forgetting the embedding (incidence records what is related, not how far or at what angle). A quantity not invariant under a symmetry of the input cannot be a function of the input alone: dimensionful constants are not scale-invariant, signs are not reflection-invariant, metric data is not embedding-invariant. What survives the full symmetry group is exactly dimensionless ratios and symmetry-allowed forms.

**M.CW-a — Pullback-flatness (R1).** A connection *defined* as the record of a frame map, `A = g⁻¹dg`, has curvature `F = dA + A∧A ≡ 0` (Maurer–Cartan). A "gauge field obtained by varying a geometric quantity" is pure gauge — zero field strength, no dynamics.

**M.CW-b — Arity wall (R1 for forms).** A k-body exchange contributes a term of multilinearity k: two-body exchange gives only bilinear (kinetic/mass) terms; a cubic potential needs a 3-body vertex or a loop. The determinant — the unique holomorphic cubic SU(3) invariant on the **6** — is irreducibly 3-fold (`cos 3α`) and cannot arise from any 4-fold (π/8) operation. Form is import-free; coefficient and sign are not.

**M.CW-c — Metric-free combinatorics carry no moments (R2).** A graph specified only by incidence (bipartite, triangle-free, no bond vectors — e.g. Heawood) has no geometric moments to integrate against; reading a stiffness, tension, or oriented coefficient off it returns nothing or a sign fixed by the arbitrary realization.

**Use.** M.CW is the mechanism behind Vocabulary Substitution. When an entry claims to *derive* a quantity from a discrete/combinatorial structure, classify the target first: a dimensionless ratio or allowed form is admissible; a dimensionful constant, metric/signature, or sign is an import and must be declared (Prior Address) or the entry is making an M.CW error. Run this filter *before* the Eddington check — it catches over-reach at the level of *what kind of quantity* is being claimed. *(Forward pointer, V4.44: when the target is not a derived quantity but a **structural identification** of a physical object with the combinatorial one, the per-axis admissibility test is **M.REL (Relational Admissibility)** below — it isolates which of scale / metric / sign / ontology the identification crosses and files the cleared residual at R2.)*

**Does NOT claim.** Not that the substrate has no metric/scale/sign — only that those enter as posited structure, not as combinatorial outputs. Not a devaluation of the framework's combinatorial results (dimensionless physics from combinatorics is the admissible side). Not a verdict on any specific entry; a filter to apply. Cross-refs: Vocabulary Substitution; Prior Address Standard; §3.A.1/§3.A.3 (prior bridge failures as instances); §2.84 (M.CW-b instance); §4.14 Item 1 (open M.CW tension on the 3+1 signature claim).

### The Observable-Bridge Asymmetry (M.BRIDGE)

*(Methodological note, June 1, 2026. R2 — an empirical generalization over the program's own audited history; defeasible, not a theorem.)*

**Statement.** Across audited history, framework-internal mathematics has survived adversarial audit; every bridge from that mathematics to a dimensionful physical observable that has reached audit has required an import it could not derive, and has then been retired or held as an unexplained anomaly. Stated as a prior, not a verdict: it does not say a physical bridge can never be derived; it says that to date the secure contributions have been mathematical and the observable bridges have not earned their numbers from within the framework.

**Instances.** Retired/thinned bridges: §3.A.1 (E₈→H₄ engine, glueball), §3.A.3 (sin²(πU/4) α-decay; the three-regime finding reduced on audit to one real break at Z=88 with a conventional octupole-deformation explanation), §3.A.5 (SQT-Info, 0/3), §3.A.6 (SQT-QCD), §3.A.8 (meson bridge), ferromagnetism (Gate-1 spin-flip, refuted, R3). Surviving math: §1.1 (PSL(2,7) spectral rigidity), the sedenion ZD / 42-kernel structure, the Császár combinatorics (Paper I), §2.84 Part A, the §2.7x cluster. Genuine middle case: §2.1 (mass table — an unexplained numerical anomaly, the only honest occupant of "Empirical Anomaly"). The source session's "two bridges" is corrected by this enumeration, not by a different count.

**Unifying reading.** This is M.CW at program scale. The surviving mathematics lives on the admissible side of the wall (forms, ratios, group/incidence structure); every observable bridge requires crossing it (a scale, sign, or spectrum), and that crossing is where the import enters. So the asymmetry is not evidence the physics is *false* — it is the wall expressing itself sector by sector.

**Constructive consequence.** The citable contributions to date are the mathematical ones (§1.1 is the external-facing exemplar). Forward discipline: before claiming a bridge to an observable, name the import — the specific scale, sign, or spectrum it requires — and show its prior address; absent that, the bridge is an M.CW crossing without a ticket and will not survive audit.

**Does NOT claim.** No specific open sector is doomed (it shifts a prior, adjudicates nothing). "Survived audit so far" is a statement about evidence, not ultimate truth. Not a retraction or closure; no register changes because of this note.

### Relational Admissibility (M.REL)

*(Methodological clarification, June 18, 2026. R2 — a precision on the admissible side of M.CW, strictly subordinate to it; not a relaxation of M.CW or M.BRIDGE. **This corrects an unfiled June-18 draft** whose premise — "unit-invariant relationships are a free admissible category" — over-broadened the admissible side: unit-invariance covers only the **rescaling** symmetry of M.CW's invariance argument, not the **reflection/relabeling** and **forget-the-embedding** symmetries that gate signs and metrics. The draft was never folded, so this is the first M.REL of record. Sibling to M.CW / M.BRIDGE / M.ONT; downstream of M.CW-c and the I4 declaration (§2.88.E).)*

**Statement.** Not every import is a scale import. M.CW blocks four kinds — a **dimensionful constant**, a **metric** (distance, angle, signature), a **sign** (orientation, chirality, coupling sign), and, via M.ONT, the **energy functional / topological invariant** the object carries. A structural identification between a mathematical object and a physical one is admissible — citable at R2 without an import — exactly when the relationship it asserts is a function of the **combinatorial / topological / group data alone**: invariant under all three symmetries of the M.CW invariance argument simultaneously — global rescaling (no scale), reflection/relabeling (no sign), and forgetting the embedding (no metric). The test is **per-axis**. Clear the identification on scale, metric, sign, and ontology separately; the residual that crosses none of the four is the admissible content, and it is real physical content. Unit-invariance alone is **necessary but not sufficient** — it clears only the scale axis.

**The three-step decomposition (a diagnostic, not a license).** M.CW + M.BRIDGE are sometimes read as "block any step that will eventually need a scale." That over-blocks: it kills an admissible topological/group correspondence because a *later* metric step exists. Separating the steps lets the admissible part be filed and each import isolated.

- **Step 1 — mathematical result (R1).** The geometry produces a relationship in the discrete data. π₁(S¹) = ℤ. The Fano plane has 7 lines. p6m has exactly 2 isotropic rank-4 invariants. No import.
- **Step 2 — structural identification (R2-eligible, conditional on per-axis clearance).** A physical object is identified with the mathematical one and the *form* of the physical constraint is asserted to match the form of the mathematical one. **Step 2 is not automatically import-free.** It can still carry a metric, a sign, or an ontology, and those must be decomposed out, not assumed absent. The admissible residual is only the part that clears all four axes.
- **Step 3 — metric/scale claim (R3 pending a prior address).** The object has a specific value in units (r = ξ_phys = 0.358 l_P; the couplings κ, G) — or a specific *dimensionless* value (ζ, α⁻¹). M.BRIDGE applies here in full.

**The per-axis import test.** For the relationship a candidate Step-2 identification claims, ask: **Scale** — does it name a dimensionful magnitude, *or fix a pure number to a specific value*? (A specific value of a dimensionless number — ζ, α⁻¹ — is Step-3-class even though it carries no unit.) **Metric** — does it depend on a distance, an angle, or a signature? (2π, any R/r ratio, the 1/r² *exponent*, any length or angle. M.CW-c: metric-free combinatorics carry no moments.) **Sign** — does it depend on an orientation, a chirality, or the sign of a coupling? (M.CW: combinatorics cannot fix a sign.) **Ontology** — does its truth depend on which energy functional / topological invariant the object carries? (M.ONT: ropelength vs Hopf charge are not energy-identifiable.) The admissible Step-2 content is what survives all four — unit-invariant *and* reflection-invariant *and* embedding-invariant *and* ontology-robust.

**Worked examples (corrected).** **2π closure:** import-free content is π₁(S¹) = ℤ — the vortex closes, winding number 1, a *count*; the constant **2π is metric** (circumference/radius is Euclidean; on S² a great circle's circumference-to-geodesic-radius ratio is not 2π), so "the vortex closes / winding 1" is admissible Step-2 while "the closure budget is 2π" crosses the metric axis and needs the flat-metric (or specific-lattice) import — exactly the **count-vs-metric** distinction that decides whether the §2.50 gate can close combinatorially (M.REL preserves that discrimination, it does not dissolve it). **§2.90 1/r²:** the admissible Step-2 content is the incidence relation (lattice connectivity forces amplitude to fall with shell distance, a monotone relation in the graph data); the **exponent 2 is an import** — I4, three propagating dimensions (§2.88.E: "the 1/r² exponent is dimension-sourced, M.CW; a 2D substrate would give 1/r"), so §2.90's inverse-square is admissible-relation **+** declared-I4 import, *not* import-free, with the coupling scale (κ, G) the further Step-3 gap. **§1.1 (PSL(2,7) spectral rigidity):** this is **Step 1**, not Step 2 — a theorem about a mathematical object's symmetry structure making no dimensionful physical claim; it survived audit because it *stayed at* Step 1 (a genuine Step-2 reading, "the physical system has this symmetry," is available and would be R2, but that is not what carried it through audit).

**Register.** Step 1: R1. Step 2: R2 — **no new register is needed**; R2 is *defined* as a structural observation with R1 targets named, which is exactly a cleared Step-2 identification. Step 3: R3 pending a Step-3 prior address. M.REL therefore changes no register and opens no category; it is a **filing rule** — decompose per axis, file the cleared residual at R2, isolate each import with its Step-3 target.

**Why the motivating frustration is mostly misattributed.** The bridges M.BRIDGE has actually retired or walled are Step-3 *values*: ζ = 1 − π/√12 (G-ζ1), the §2.1 mass numbers, the gravity coupling. R2 already houses Step-2 identifications — §2.50.A (electron = 2π first-stable-closure, with the topological-trap mechanism) is filed R2 *today*. The wall has not been eating clean Step-2 identifications; it has been eating Step-3 numbers, correctly. The cure is not a new license but the discipline of decomposing — so a Step-2 identification is filed at R2 with its imports named, rather than over-blocked or waved through whole.

**Use.** When an entry claims a physical identification: (1) write the relationship as a function of the combinatorial/topological/group data and check it clears all four axes; (2) file the cleared residual at R2 as a structural identification with its falsification path (the topology/symmetry could fail to match); (3) name each crossed axis as a separate import with its Step-3 target; (4) run this **after** M.CW (which classifies the quantity) and **before** the Eddington check. The Step-2/Step-3 conflation, *and* treating a Step-2 form as a derivation of a Step-3 value, are both the Eddington Maneuver at the structural level once a Step-3 value is fit and then justified by the Step-2 form.

**Relation to M.CW / M.BRIDGE / M.ONT.** Downstream of M.CW-c (why a ratio of lengths/angles is not admissible) and the I4 declaration (why the 1/r² exponent is an import). Does not weaken M.BRIDGE: dimensionful observable bridges still require imports, and a Step-2 identification is not such a bridge. Bounded by M.ONT: an identification whose truth depends on the energy functional is ontology-gated until M.ONT is declared.

**Does NOT claim.** That unit-invariance suffices for admissibility (it clears only the scale axis; the criterion is all-four-axes / expressible-in-the-discrete-data-alone). That every structural identification is valid (the topology/symmetry must actually match — a substantive check). That Step 2 closes a physical question (Step 3 is still required for any dimensionful *or specific-dimensionless* prediction). That M.CW or M.BRIDGE is overstated (both are correctly stated; M.REL names the admissible residual and the per-axis decomposition more precisely). No register changes; no entry reclassified by this note.

### Literature-Search-First (search at the conjecture stage)

*(Standing workflow rule, June 18, 2026 — added after the third prior-art collision in the framework's history (§2.78 / V4.15, and now the pathion / PG(n−1,2) ZD recursion, V4.41→V4.42 prior-art correction). A diligence rule, sibling to the Eddington Maneuver and Vocabulary Substitution, but on the **novelty** axis rather than the soundness axis.)*

**Statement.** Run a literature search **at the conjecture stage — before any audit or compute investment** — triggered automatically by (a) any **named structure** appearing, especially one already cited in the project files (e.g. “box-kite,” “assessor,” “pathion,” “Pléiades” — all de Marrais / Moreno coinages); (b) any result that **“connects” two established mathematical objects**; (c) any result that **feels clean or general enough to publish**. Deep-audit effort (longhand proofs, line-by-line verification, two-leg / field-class checks) is reserved for questions a literature check has **already shown to be open**.

**Why.** Rigor on the *soundness* axis (is the computation correct?) does not substitute for diligence on the *novelty* axis (is the result new?) — and novelty is what determines whether a result is publishable at all. The search-before-build step has failed three times here; the cost each time is the author's compute and time spent on a deep audit of a true-but-known result. The trigger is cheap (one search); the miss is expensive.

**Relation to the other disciplines.** Distinct from the Prior Address Standard (whether a *constant* is derived vs. fitted) and the Eddington Maneuver (post-hoc correction-fitting): this rule governs whether a *theorem-shaped claim* is checked against the literature before it is invested in. The standing §2.78 annotation (“a second-order instance of the V4.14 pattern”) is the record that this collision recurs.

*Refinement (June 18, 2026, V4.45 — cross-dialect search): the trigger extends to searching the **object's canonical names across adjacent communities**, not only the framing's own terms. A diligent literature search in one community's vocabulary can miss a complete classification filed under another's — the OP-PSL.3 / spectral-rigidity case, where the paper's "spectral rigidity / coset Laplacian / Cheeger / crystallization" frame does not surface the Gelfand-pair / multiplicity-free / distance-transitive classification of the same object (L²(G/H) multiplicity-free *is* a Gelfand pair). Recognizing the object under the owning community's name is the translation key; this is the same vocabulary-gap pattern as the V4.42 box-kite / assessor / pathion prior art. See the V4.45 record.*

#### Statement (R1)

The K₇ (Császár polyhedron) symmetry group is PSL(2,7). Its spin double cover is SL(2,7), with |SL(2,7)| = 336. The irreducible complex representations of SL(2,7) split into two classes by the action of the central element −I:

- **Six irreps factoring through PSL(2,7)** (where −I acts as +1): dimensions 1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 8.
- **Five genuine spin irreps** (where −I acts as −1): dimensions 4, 4, 6, 6, 8.

(Sum of squares: 168 + 168 = 336 over 11 irreps, matching the 11 conjugacy classes verified by direct enumeration in §2.77.)

**No 2-dimensional faithful complex irrep of SL(2,7) exists.** The smallest genuine spin irreps are 4-dimensional.

#### Proof (divisor enumeration — strictly self-contained)

The non-existence of a faithful 2D irrep follows from finite-group theory without external table lookup. The argument:

**Step 1 (Schur orthogonality).** The regular representation of SL(2,7) decomposes as Σ d_i² = |G| = 336, with one d_i per irrep. SL(2,7) has 11 conjugacy classes (verified by direct orbit enumeration over the 336 elements with ad − bc ≡ 1 mod 7), so exactly 11 irreps.

**Step 2 (PSL/spin split by central character).** Irreps of SL(2,7) on which −I acts trivially factor through PSL(2,7); those on which −I acts as −1 are genuine spin irreps. PSL(2,7) has six irreps with dimensions {1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 8} (sum of squares = 1 + 9 + 9 + 36 + 49 + 64 = 168, verified directly from the PSL(2,7) class structure). The remaining 11 − 6 = 5 irreps are genuine spin, with Σ d_i² = 336 − 168 = 168.

**Step 3 (Divisor constraint).** Each irrep dimension d divides |G| = 336 (standard consequence of Schur's lemma and the fact that the center of the group algebra acts on each irrep by scalars). The divisors of 336 are {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 12, 14, 16, 21, 24, 28, 42, 48, 56, 84, 112, 168, 336}.

**Step 4 (Diophantine enumeration).** Enumerate all 5-tuples (d₁ ≤ d₂ ≤ d₃ ≤ d₄ ≤ d₅) of divisors of 336 with Σ d_i² = 168. The constraint d₅² ≤ 168 forces d₅ ≤ 12, restricting candidates to divisors {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 12}. Direct enumeration:

| d₅ = 12: | 12² = 144; need 24 from 4 terms with each ≤ 12. | Best 4-tuple sums: max 4·144 = 576, min is 1²·4 = 4. Need exact 24. 24 = 16+4+4+0 (no zero allowed); 24 = 16+4+1+? (16+4+1+3 = 24 ✓ with terms 4,2,1,? — but √3 not a divisor); 24 = 9+9+1+? no; etc. **No valid 5-tuple with d₅ = 12.** |
| d₅ = 8: | 64; need 104 from 4 terms each ≤ 8. Candidates use d_i ∈ {1,2,3,4,6,7,8}. **(8,6,6,4,4):** 64+36+36+16+16 = 168 ✓. Check all smaller starts: (8,8,6,?,?) needs 32 from 2 terms ≤ 6 from {1,4,9,16,36}: no. (8,7,?,?,?) needs 55 from 3 terms ≤ 7: 49+4+? = 53+? = 55? No. (8,6,6,?,?) needs 32 from 2 terms ≤ 6: 16+16 ✓, gives (8,6,6,4,4). |
| d₅ = 7: | 49; need 119 from 4 terms ≤ 7. Max 4·49 = 196, min sufficient. 119 = 49+49+? not enough room since two 7s = 98, need 21 from 2 terms ≤ 7: no. 119 = 49+36+? = 85+? need 34 from 2: no. **None.** |
| d₅ ≤ 6: | Max Σ d_i² ≤ 5·36 = 180; need 168. Candidates: (6,6,6,6,6) = 180 ≠ 168. (6,6,6,6,?) needs −12: impossible. **None.** |

**Unique solution:** (d₁, d₂, d₃, d₄, d₅) = (4, 4, 6, 6, 8).

**Conclusion:** No 2 appears in the genuine spin irrep dimension list. Combined with the PSL-factor list {1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 8}, no 2 appears in any irrep dimension of SL(2,7). **SL(2,7) admits no faithful 2-dimensional complex irreducible representation.** ∎

The argument uses only Schur orthogonality, the order |G| = 336, the |PSL(2,7)| = 168 split, and divisor enumeration. No external character table is consulted.

#### Framework consequence

Any SQT argument that informally invokes a "K₇ spinor doublet" — a 2-component spinor object transforming under the K₇ symmetry group's spin double cover — is using language that **does not match the actual representation theory**. The native K₇ spinor object is 4-dimensional.

This is structurally analogous to the relativistic Dirac bispinor (which is also 4-dimensional, with a chirality label distinguishing left and right Weyl 2-component pieces) rather than to the non-relativistic Pauli spinor doublet (2-dimensional, no internal chirality).

**V4.7 update (May 27, 2026):** The "structurally analogous to relativistic Dirac bispinor" wording above is **superseded** by the WD-1.a explicit-matrix-construction finding (`clifford_hunt.py`, `cl02_correction.py`; see §2.E-WD closure section in Cluster L). σ₄ does NOT natively harbor the Cℓ(1,3) Dirac Clifford algebra: the 42 candidate γ⁵-like operators Γ_x = −iσ₄(x) from order-4 elements x ∈ SL(2,7) furnish 168 anticommuting pairs but ZERO mutually anticommuting quadruples. The 112 anticommuting triples all satisfy Γ₁Γ₂Γ₃ = ±i·I₄ (scalar volume), so they are Cℓ(0,2) generator pairs with one derived element, not independent Cℓ(0,3) generators. By Schur's lemma on the irreducible σ₄, any operator commuting with the SL(2,7) action must be scalar — which forecloses the chirality decomposition required for a Dirac bispinor structure. The accurate structural analogy is to the **complexified quaternionic 1-spinor** (Cℓ(0,2) ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ acting on a 2-dim quaternionic = 4-dim complex space), not to the Dirac bispinor (Cℓ(1,3) acting on ℂ⁴). The R1 load-bearing claim of this entry — no faithful 2D irrep of SL(2,7); divisor-enumeration proof above — is preserved unchanged. Only the Dirac-vs-Pauli interpretive analogy is corrected: the framework's native K₇-spinor object is 4D quaternionic, not 4D Dirac. The §2.D-FC "What this entry does NOT claim" list (item 1: framework's 4D spinors NOT claimed to carry standard Lorentz-bispinor structure) anticipated this correction; V4.7 makes the structural specification (quaternionic, not Dirac) explicit.

#### Audit implications

Three classes of prior SQT content require audit against this constraint:

1. **Direct invocations of "K₇ spinor doublet" or "fundamental spinor of K₇"**: These are using a representation that does not exist. They must be either (a) reframed in terms of 4D bispinors, or (b) shown to refer to a different mathematical object than the K₇ symmetry-group spin reps.

2. **Cross-references between K₇ spin structure and SU(2) spin-½**: SU(2) and SL(2,7) are different groups with different representation theories. SU(2) has a faithful 2-dim irrep (the fundamental); SL(2,7) does not. Any framework argument that pulls SU(2) spin-½ structure into the K₇ spin reps must specify the bridging mechanism explicitly, because it is not automatic.

3. **The ferromagnetism conjecture's reframed Gate 1 Condition 1** (per `unaudited_conjecture_incomplete_closure_ferromagnetism.md`): the "spin-flip on a doublet" reading is refuted by this constraint and the parent §2.77.

Audit of prior content for these patterns is logged as OP-2.77-FB in §2.77 Part VIII.

#### What this entry does NOT claim

- Does NOT claim that the framework's 4D spinor objects carry standard Lorentz-bispinor structure. Whether they do is the substance of §2.E-WD.
- Does NOT claim that SU(2) spin-½ is absent from the framework. SU(2) may appear via a different group-theoretic route (e.g., as a piece of a larger structure that contains SL(2,7) as a subgroup), but it does not arise from the K₇ spin double cover as a fundamental rep.
- Does NOT claim that the K₇-bispinor structure is "relativistic" in the sense of carrying a 4-momentum. The structural analogy to Dirac bispinors is at the level of "4-component spinor with chirality label," not at the level of "spinor on Minkowski space."

#### Methodological note

This entry exists as a separate Cluster D filing (rather than only inside §2.77 in Cluster L) because the constraint applies framework-wide and downstream entries need to cite it directly without depending on the chirality-rep apparatus of §2.77. The constraint is one numerical fact (the irrep dimensions of SL(2,7)) elevated to a framework-level audit obligation. The divisor-enumeration proof above replaces the original V4.6 merge-patch wording (which cited ATLAS data for 2·L₂(7)) with a strictly self-contained Diophantine argument, ensuring no external table dependency.

## E. Cayley-Dickson Tower and Hexagonal Vacuum

### §2.22 Cayley-Dickson Torus Fold Series

**Construction (R2).** The p6m planar lattice admits a series of quotients indexed by Cayley-Dickson imaginary count: ℝ → ℂ → ℍ → 𝕆 → 𝕊 (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 imaginaries, summing to 30 imaginaries plus 1 real = 31 = 2⁵ − 1 generators). At each doubling, the p6m fundamental domain folds and the resulting quotient surface acquires the algebraic structure of the next CD level. The fold-series geometry is the substrate-level realization of the Hurwitz division-algebra sequence.

The series terminates at sedenions because the CD doubling beyond 𝕊 produces algebras with zero divisors that fail the division property; the framework reading is that the sedenion stage is the boundary of the structural cascade and the appearance of zero-divisors at this rung is not a defect but a structural feature (the ZD geometry is what carries the Fano-line classifier in §§2.55, 2.58.B, 2.62).

### §2.23 PSL Symmetry vs. Clifford Capacity: Methodological Distinction

**Principle (R2).** Two algebraic registers act on the framework's geometric content and must not be conflated:

- **PSL column** answers **symmetry / combinatorial** questions: orbits, transformation relationships, how objects move under group actions. Relevant numbers: 7, 21, 168.
- **Clifford column** answers **capacity** questions: algebraic room, spinor content, how much structure a given algebraic level can hold. Relevant numbers: 4, 16, 64, 84, 256.

The two columns ask different kinds of questions about the same geometry. The PSL/Cl pairing breaks at Rung 3: Cl(8) cannot represent the 7+1 split natural to PSL(2,7); the natural partner is Cl(7).

Looking for cos(18°) in the (2,3,7) hyperbolic triangle / Rung 3 geometry is the canonical confusion this distinction prevents — cos(18°) lives at Rung 2 (pentagon / A₅ level) and arrives at Rung 3 via face inheritance, not via Rung 3 geometry directly.

### §2.24 p6m Vacuum Frustration Constant T

**Definition.** T = 1 − 3 tan²(π/7) ≈ 0.3043.

**Origin (R1).** The p6m planar lattice carries a hexagonal/triangular dual structure. At each hexagonal vertex, three triangles meet; the deviation between the hexagonal interior angle and the heptagonal frustration angle generates a residual constant T. The expression 1 − 3 tan²(π/7) is the closed form of this residual; no fit parameters.

**Status.** T is a vacuum constant of the p6m lattice, not specific to any particular embedding. It appears in the substrate-level descriptions of vacuum frustration, crossing tax, and the K₇,₇-minus-matching graph automorphism content (S₇ ≀ ℤ₂).

### §2.26 Vacuum Ground State Selection: p6m as Survivor of Chaos Competition

**Theorem 2.1 (R2, reframed).** Among all wallpaper groups admitting a hexagonal sub-symmetry under chaos competition (random-perturbation selection in a coupled-oscillator lattice), **p6m survives uniquely**. The flat p6m lattice has no layered structure until a fold is applied. The "layers" of the framework's geometric content (vacuum / boundary / outer-shell / etc.) emerge only after a fold threshold is crossed.

**§2.26.OP1 (open problem).** Identify the explicit fold threshold and the projection map under which p6m generates the Császár torus as the boundary cross-section. See §2.63 for a related angle-dependent re-reading conjecture.

### §2.27 Tension-Snap as Universal Mechanism

**Principle (R2).** CD doublings and fold thresholds are the same class of event: a tension that has accumulated against a structural constraint releases discontinuously when the constraint can no longer hold. The primitives of the snap event are (0, 1) — the state before and after — with no intermediate continuous interpolation. The "snap conditional" (that snap occurs under sufficient tension) is not universal; specific tension thresholds depend on the structural register (CD rung, fold geometry, K₇ packing density).

**Scope boundary.** Tension-snap is a class of event, not a derivation of any specific physical quantity. It organizes related phenomena (CD doubling, fold threshold, cosmological phase transition per §4.11) under a single structural pattern.

### §2.28 Metastable Knot Admissibility

**Principle (R2).** A knot configuration is admissible in the framework if it is topologically stable on confinement timescales, not if it minimizes ropelength. The framework's stabilizer values Z_f and the knot-to-particle mapping (§2.1) reflect metastable topological stability, not unique ropelength minima. The distinction matters for the top-quark assignment problem (§4.7): a knot configuration may be admissible at metastable stability even when an alternative knot achieves shorter ropelength.

### §2.30 Two-Layer Structure of Three-Strand Configurations

**Observation (R2).** The three Borromean strands carry both **discrete heptagonal/octonionic content** (handled by the F₇* unification: Cl(7) grade structure, canonical edge ↔ non-face triangle bijection, Z₇ ⋊ Z₆ Császár symmetry) and a **continuous Euclidean envelope** (each strand circumscribed by a circle). The two layers coexist on the same three-strand configurations and are bridged by **circumscription**.

In the planar projection where three circumscribed circles are pairwise tangent, they satisfy the classical half-angle tangent identity

$$\tan(A/2)\tan(B/2) + \tan(B/2)\tan(C/2) + \tan(C/2)\tan(A/2) = 1$$

with controlled approximation error governed by the inscribed-heptagon sagitta ε_sagitta = R − R cos(π/7) ≈ 0.099 R.

| Layer | Content | Machinery |
|-------|---------|-----------|
| Discrete | Heptagonal/octonionic | F₇* unification (Cl(7), Császár, Fano) |
| Continuous | Euclidean envelope | Half-angle tangent identity on circumscribed circles |
| Bridge | Circumscription | Sagitta correction ≈ 0.099 R |

**What is claimed.** Two layers coexist; the bridge has a named, computable approximation error; the continuous layer satisfies a known classical identity.

**What is NOT claimed.** Not a new structural derivation. Not a claim that the half-angle identity *implies* the F₇* structure or vice versa. Not a claim that 0.099 R is sharp or has physical significance.

That route has been closed with a negative finding (see §3.06). ### §2.70 S₃-Equivariant Homomorphism Rigidity: π₁(S³\B) → F₇*

*Status update (V4.3 fold-in, May 25, 2026):* Verification check CLOSED. SQT audit confirmed that "F₇*" in the §2.15 proof sketch refers strictly to the multiplicative group of the field 𝔽₇, i.e., F₇* = (ℤ/7ℤ)* ≅ ℤ/6ℤ. This group is abelian by definition. Aut(ℤ/6ℤ) ≅ ℤ/2 and gcd(|A₃|, |Aut(F₇*)|) = gcd(3, 2) = 1, forcing the A₃ ⊂ S₃ action on F₇* to be trivially rigid. No richer non-abelian structure is involved at this layer; none was ever claimed. The rigidity theorem of §2.70 holds without qualification. **§2.70 status: Register 1, unconditional.**


**Date:** May 24, 2026. **Register:** R1, modulo one verification check on the meaning of "F₇*" in the §2.15 proof sketch's actual target (see "Verification check pending" below). If the verification confirms F₇* is the bare multiplicative group of 𝔽₇ (cyclic of order 6), the result is unconditionally R1.

**Status.** Supports §2.15's flavor-blindness clause from an independent group-theoretic route. Closes the F₇*-image layer as a candidate location for topological strand-distinction.

**Statement.** Any S₃-equivariant homomorphism

$$\varphi : \pi_1(S^3 \setminus B) \to F_7^*$$

(where B denotes the Borromean rings and S₃ acts on the source by permuting the three meridian generators a, b, c) factors through the abelianization H₁(S³ \ B) = ℤ³ and sends all three meridian classes to the same element of F₇*. Equivalently: under the equivariance constraint, the homomorphism cannot distinguish the three strands at the F₇*-image layer.

**Proof.**

1. **Factorization through abelianization.** F₇* is abelian. Any homomorphism from a group to an abelian group factors through the abelianization of the source. Therefore φ factors as π₁(S³ \ B) → H₁(S³ \ B) = ℤ³ → F₇* with the first arrow the Hurewicz map and the second a homomorphism of abelian groups. Write the images of the three meridian classes [a], [b], [c] as α, β, γ ∈ F₇* respectively.

2. **S₃ acts on the source by permuting meridians.** The 3-cycle subgroup A₃ ⊂ S₃ cyclically rotates them: (123): ([a], [b], [c]) ↦ ([b], [c], [a]).

3. **Available S₃-action on the target.** F₇* ≅ ℤ/6 as a group. Aut(ℤ/6) = (ℤ/6)* = {1, 5} ≅ ℤ/2, generated by inversion x ↦ x⁻¹. Therefore Aut(F₇*) ≅ ℤ/2.

4. **A₃ acts trivially on the target.** Any homomorphism A₃ → Aut(F₇*) is a map from a group of order 3 to a group of order 2. Since gcd(3, 2) = 1, the only such homomorphism is trivial.

5. **Equivariance forces strand equivalence on the image.** Under the 3-cycle (123), equivariance requires (α, β, γ) = (β, γ, α) in the target. Since A₃ acts trivially on the target (step 4), this is the requirement α = β = γ. ∎

**Implications.**

*(i) Mathematical reason for §2.15's flavor-blindness.* §2.15 asserts that A(proton) = A(neutron) at leading order because "quark flavor (up vs. down) assigns quantum numbers to components but does not alter the linking topology." This entry supplies an elementary group-theoretic reason why the F₇*-image layer could not distinguish the strands even if asked to: the relevant target's automorphism group has order coprime to the cyclic-rotation order of the strands.

*(ii) Z_f = 6 corresponds to the primitive-root case.* With α = β = γ, the image of φ is the cyclic subgroup ⟨α⟩ ⊆ F₇*. Its order divides 6 and equals: 1 if α = 1; 2 if α = 6 ≡ −1; 3 if α ∈ {2, 4}; 6 if α ∈ {3, 5} (primitive root; full F₇*). The Z_f = 6 result of the §2.15 proof sketch corresponds to the last case: all three meridians map identically to a primitive root of F₇*.

*(iii) Strand-distinguishing mechanisms cannot live at this layer.* Candidate alternative locations, if such a mechanism is to exist anywhere in the framework's machinery: (a) Massey-product structure of the Borromean link beyond H₁; (b) homomorphisms to non-abelian targets such as PSL(2,7), where the rigidity argument does not apply because Aut order is not coprime to 3; (c) explicit non-equivariant constructions. None of these is in the §2.15 proof sketch's current F₇* machinery. Each is an open candidate location, not a present result.

**Verification check pending before unconditional R1 filing.** This result assumes "F₇*" in the §2.15 proof sketch refers to the bare cyclic group of order 6, i.e., the multiplicative group of the field 𝔽₇. The eight-step proof sketch should be cross-checked: if "F₇*" is shorthand for a richer non-abelian structure carrying F₇* only as a quotient, the rigidity argument may not apply and the analysis must be redone with the correct target.

**What this does NOT claim.**
- Does not derive Z_f = 6 (only identifies which case of the S₃-equivariant homomorphism Z_f = 6 corresponds to).
- Does not address whether the §2.15 proof sketch's remaining seven steps are correct (only the S₃-equivariance step is treated here).
- Does not address the Massey-product or PSL(2,7) routes (open candidate locations, not present results).
- Does not produce or rule out a 1+2 strand splitting *anywhere* in the framework — only at the F₇*-image layer of the abelianized link group.

**Methodological note.** The conclusion is framework-supportive; that pattern is the one most susceptible to Eddington Maneuver, and the result was checked under that filter. The derivation runs forward from group-theoretic axioms (the Hurewicz map, the structure of Aut(ℤ/6), the order argument) without consulting §2.15's empirical performance. The conclusion is a constraint that *happens* to be consistent with the framework's existing commitments; it is not pre-tuned to them. No experimental quantity is consulted at any step.

### §2.71 S₃ Orbit Structure on PG(2,2) under PSL(2,7) Action: The 3+3+1 Partition

**Date:** May 24, 2026. **Register split:** Part I (computation and strand-distinction implication) — R1 (elementary group theory). Part II (open structural question on the second 3-orbit and singleton, candidate framework-internal locations to check) — R2. Part III (three speculative interpretations) — R3, explicitly flagged for vigilance, no structural use sanctioned.

**Status.** Closes the second of two natural candidate locations for topological strand-distinction at the PSL(2,7) layer. Companion to §2.70 (which closes the F₇*-image layer).

**Statement (R1).** For any subgroup S₃ ⊂ PSL(2,7) acting on the 7 points of the Fano plane PG(2,2), the orbit structure is **3 + 3 + 1**:
- One orbit of size 3 (regular S₃-action)
- A second orbit of size 3 (distinct as a subset of PG(2,2), isomorphic as an S₃-set)
- One fixed point (singleton orbit)

The partition is forced by the structure of PSL(2,7) and is independent of the choice of S₃ conjugacy class.

**Proof.**

1. **Element orders in PSL(2,7).** PSL(2,7) has order 168 = 2³ × 3 × 7 with element orders {1, 2, 3, 4, 7}. Any S₃ contains an element of order 3.

2. **Action of an order-3 element on 7 points.** Cycle structure consists of 3-cycles and fixed points. The only partition of 7 into parts of size 1 and 3 is 3 + 3 + 1.

3. **Refinement by S₃.** The involutions of S₃ invert the 3-cycle and therefore preserve each 3-cycle setwise (cannot swap the two 3-orbits, as that would conjugate the 3-cycle to a 3-cycle on a different set of points, not to its own inverse).

4. **Conjugacy independence.** PSL(2,7) acts 2-transitively on PG(2,2). All order-3 elements form a single conjugacy class. S₃ subgroups are determined up to conjugacy by their order-3 elements together with the choice of inverting involution. Therefore the 3+3+1 partition is structurally independent of the specific S₃ chosen. ∎

**Explicit construction.** PG(2,2) = (𝔽₂³ \ {0})/scalars. Pick a Fano line ℓ = {P₁, P₂, P₃} = {(1,0,0), (0,1,0), (1,1,0)} (the line z = 0). Take S₃ ⊂ PSL(2,7) ≅ GL(3,2) to be the subgroup of matrices

$$\begin{pmatrix} a & b & 0 \\ c & d & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

where the upper-left 2×2 block runs over GL(2,2) ≅ S₃, permuting {P₁, P₂, P₃} in all six ways. Direct computation gives orbits {P₁, P₂, P₃}, {Q₂, Q₃, Q₄} (the three Fano points with z = 1 other than the affine origin), {Q₁ = (0,0,1)} (the affine origin).

**Implication for strand-distinction.** If the three Borromean strands of §2.15 embed as the three points of a Fano line ℓ (a natural embedding given the link's 3-component structure and PG(2,2)'s 3-point lines), then under any S₃ ⊂ PSL(2,7) the strands remain in a single S₃-orbit (no 1+2 split). The action produces a second 3-orbit (geometric structure off the line, not on it) and one fixed point (the affine origin relative to the chosen line). The strands do not undergo a 1+2 symmetry reduction at this layer.

**Independence from the embedding choice.** The conjugacy-independence in step 4 means the 3+3+1 partition cannot be circumvented by a different choice of S₃ inside PSL(2,7), or by a different choice of which Fano line to use as the strand image. This is genuine architectural rigidity at the PSL(2,7) layer.

**Open structural question (R2).** What, if anything, in the framework's existing machinery corresponds to the second 3-orbit and the singleton? The question is well-formed and can be answered by working forward from existing §-entries without consulting any empirical target. Candidate framework-internal locations to check for independent appearance of 3+3+1-style structure:
- §2.25's universal −2 scalar anchor (dim-zero kernel of APS boundary operator on Császár torus; structurally a single scalar, at least dimensionally compatible with a singleton orbit)

- §2.68.7's 49-pair verification of the doubling axis ⟨e₀, e₈⟩ (a distinguished 2D subspace; check whether 3+3 / singleton structure appears)

Independent appearance of 3+3+1 in any of these would constitute prior address for an identification. Without such independent appearance, no identification is made.

**R3 interpretive notes — FLAGGED FOR VIGILANCE.** The following are speculative and recorded with explicit Eddington-risk flags. None has prior address. None is sanctioned for structural use.

The Fano plane has a natural point-line duality, but that is not the same as particle-antiparticle duality. Importing CPT-conjugation language onto the second 3-orbit would be the Eddington Maneuver. ### §2.72 S₃ Irrep Decomposition of the §2.55 Kernel Orbit: 4·triv ⊕ 2·standard (Not 1+3)

**Date:** May 24, 2026. **Register:** R1 (linear-algebra computation, character-theoretic decomposition).

**Status.** Negative result on user-proposed 1+3 split, with positive characterization of the actual irrep structure. Filed as a companion to §2.70 and §2.71. Adds structural detail about the S₃-action on §2.55's kernel orbits without resolving any existing open problem in §2.15, §2.55, or §2.62.

**Computational basis:** `s3_kernel_action.py`, `s3_orbit_check.py`, `eight_dim_decomp.py` (May 24, 2026 session). Working ZD throughout: x = e₁ + e₁₀ ∈ 𝕊_p, sitting on Fano line L = {1, 2, 3} with missing element m = 3.

**Setup and the user-proposed hypothesis.** The hypothesis under test was: the 3+3+1 orbit structure of §2.71 lifts to a vector-space decomposition of §2.55's 4D kernel as 1D (S₃-invariant, on the affine origin Fano point 4) + 3D (carrying the standard rep of S₃, on points {5, 6, 7}). The hypothesis does not survive computation.

**Why the single 4D kernel does not decompose under S₃.** Under σ = (1 2 3) ∈ S₃, the §2.55 kernel basis for x = e₁ + e₁₀ maps as:

```
v₄ = e₇ + e₁₂     →   σ(v₄) = e₅ + e₁₂
v₅ = −e₆ + e₁₃    →   σ(v₅) = −e₇ + e₁₄
v₆ = e₅ + e₁₄     →   σ(v₆) = e₆ + e₁₅
v₇ = −e₄ + e₁₅    →   σ(v₇) = −e₄ + e₁₃
```

The original kernel spans a 4D subspace; the image under σ spans a *different* 4D subspace; together they span 8 dimensions, not 4. The S₃ action does not preserve ker(L_x) for any single ZD x, because S₃ does not fix x = e₁ + e₁₀: under (1 2 3), x ↦ e₂ + e₁₁, a different ZD on the same Fano line L. The S₃ orbit of x consists of all 6 ZDs on L:

$$\{e_1 + e_{10},\ e_1 + e_{11},\ e_2 + e_{11},\ e_2 + e_9,\ e_3 + e_9,\ e_3 + e_{10}\}$$

The stabilizer of x in S₃ is trivial because the +8 shift breaks the symmetry between the two endpoints of the bipartite edge.

**The correct S₃-invariant object: the 8D union U(L).** Collecting the 4D kernels across all 6 ZDs on line L produces an 8-dimensional invariant subspace U(L) ⊂ 𝕊_p, supported on the Fano-point complement of L (indices {4, 5, 6, 7} in Copy A and {12, 13, 14, 15} in Copy B). The S₃ permutes the 6 ZDs (the line orbit) and acts as an 8-dimensional representation on the union of their kernels.

**Character computation and irrep decomposition.** Direct computation of the character on the 8D subspace:
- χ(e) = 8
- χ(3-cycle) = 2
- χ(2-cycle) = 4

Inner products with S₃'s irreps (trivial: 1,1,1; sign: 1,1,−1; standard: 2,−1,0):

| Irrep | Multiplicity |
|---|---|
| trivial | 4 |
| sign | 0 |
| standard | 2 |

Dimension check: 4·1 + 0·1 + 2·2 = 4 + 0 + 4 = 8 ✓

**Result:**

$$U(L) \cong 4 \cdot \mathrm{triv} \oplus 0 \cdot \mathrm{sgn} \oplus 2 \cdot \mathrm{std}$$

**Geometric interpretation of the 4+0+2 structure.** The four trivial pieces are: the component along index 4 (Copy A affine origin, fixed by S₃ pointwise); the component along index 12 (Copy B affine origin, fixed because +8 shift commutes with S₃); the S₃-symmetrization of {5, 6, 7} (one invariant on Copy A's non-affine-origin 3-orbit); the S₃-symmetrization of {13, 14, 15} (the same on Copy B). The two standard pieces are: the 2D non-trivial irrep content of the S₃-action on {5, 6, 7} (Copy A); the same on {13, 14, 15} (Copy B). Equivalently: U(L) decomposes as a 2D "affine origin" subspace (S₃-invariant pointwise) + a 2D "symmetrized 3-orbit" subspace (one invariant per copy) + a 4D "non-trivial 3-orbit" subspace (two copies of the standard rep).

This is a 2 + 2 + 4 decomposition of U(L) by isotypic component, not a 1 + 3 decomposition of any single kernel.

**What this entry closes.** The hypothesis that the S₃ Borromean strand symmetry refines the §2.55 4D kernel into a 1+3 split. The 4D kernel of a single ZD is not S₃-invariant; the natural S₃-invariant object is the 8D union, and its irrep structure is 4·triv ⊕ 2·std.

**What this entry opens (or sharpens).** The 4-dimensional space of S₃-invariants on U(L) is a candidate location for any framework structure that needs to be S₃-symmetric on the line's full kernel orbit. This is *not* the same as a single ZD's kernel; its structural interpretation is open. The "affine origin" point (the S₃-fixed point of the §2.71 partition) contributes 2 of the 4 trivial pieces, distributed across Copy A and Copy B — structurally distinguished, but not in the way the original hypothesis predicted.

**Eddington-filter check.** The 4+0+2 decomposition was not a pre-stated target; it emerged from direct computation. No empirical quantity was consulted. The result is whatever the linear algebra says it is, and it differs from the user's prediction. The negative result on the user's hypothesis is filed alongside the positive characterization of what *does* happen.

**What this entry does NOT claim.**
- Does not claim physical significance for the 4·triv ⊕ 2·std decomposition. The framework's current entries do not have a derived role for "4-dim invariants on the union of kernels per Fano line"; that interpretation is open.
- Does not claim a strand-distinguishing mechanism. The 4 trivial pieces are not "one per strand"; they correspond to the 2 affine-origin coordinates plus 2 symmetrized 3-orbit coordinates, neither of which distinguishes among the 3 strands.
- Does not claim to close any open problem in §2.15, §2.55, or §2.62.

**Computational provenance files.** Three Python scripts archived in the project as the computational record for §2.72:

| Script | Function |
|---|---|
| `s3_kernel_action.py` | Tests whether the §2.55 4D kernel of x = e₁ + e₁₀ is preserved under the line-stabilizer S₃; identifies that S₃ moves x within a 6-ZD orbit |
| `s3_orbit_check.py` | Confirms the 6-element S₃-orbit of x, verifies the trivial stabilizer, computes the rank of the union of 6 4D kernels |
| `eight_dim_decomp.py` | Builds the 16×16 permutation matrices for S₃ on sedenion indices, extracts the 8×8 submatrix on indices {4,5,6,7,12,13,14,15}, computes characters and irrep multiplicities |

**Cross-references:** §2.55 (Fano-line co-line kernel structure; refined here by the per-line union analysis); §2.25.2-V (kernel rank verification, supplies the working ZD); §2.62 (TQC code spaces, structurally adjacent); §2.68 (K₇,₇ − M structural unification, doubling-axis context); §2.70 and §2.71 (same-session companion entries).

### §2.73 The 1+1+3+3 Basis Vector Extraction and Structural Origin of the Macroscopic 4-Vector

**Date filed:** May 25, 2026 (V4.3 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 2 (algebraic decomposition — unconditional) / Register 3 (physical mapping — two explicit promotion gates A and B outstanding)
**Audit:** Approved May 25, 2026. GL(3,2) geometric derivation passed unconditionally. Physical mapping section epistemic fencing confirmed.
**Cross-references:** §2.72 (4·triv ⊕ 2·std decomposition — algebraic parent), §2.70 (S₃-equivariant homomorphism rigidity), §2.71 (3+3+1 orbit structure on PG(2,2)), §2.15 (Borromean baryon S₃ symmetry).

#### Part I — Algebraic Decomposition: GL(3,2) Orbit Geometry (R2 — Unconditional)

In §2.72, the 8-dimensional space U(L) — the union of the §2.55 zero-divisor kernels across the S₃-orbit of a fixed Fano line L — was computed to decompose under the Borromean S₃ permutation symmetry as 4·triv ⊕ 2·std. The present entry extracts the 4 trivially-transforming basis vectors explicitly via the GL(3,2) finite geometry and identifies their structural origin.

**GL(3,2) orbit derivation.** |GL(3,2)| = 168. The Fano plane has 7 lines. The stabilizer of a fixed line L has index 7, hence order 168/7 = 24; this stabilizer acts as the full symmetric group S₄ on the 4 affine points off the line. Fixing one affine point P (the Pole) within this S₄ restricts to the point-stabilizer of P, which has order 24/4 = 6 — a unique S₃ subgroup. This S₃:

- Acts faithfully and transitively as the full permutation group on the 3 points of L (the Borromean strands).
- Fixes P completely.
- Acts transitively on the remaining 3 affine points (the Affine Triangle T).

Orbit partition: **1(P) + 3(L) + 3(T) = 7.** ✓ (Accounts for all Fano points.)

**Identification of the topological S₃ with the geometric S₃.** The 3 strands of the Borromean knot are identified with the 3 points of L. The topological S₃ of component permutation (§2.15, §2.70) is thereby uniquely and rigorously mapped to the GL(3,2) geometric S₃ described above. The identification is forced: the line L is the unique 3-element subset of the Fano plane on which S₃ acts as the full permutation group within the GL(3,2) structure.

**The 4 invariant basis vectors.** Taking symmetric sums over the orbits and including the globally invariant Cayley-Dickson doubling scalar e₈ (which lies outside the Fano geometry entirely):

| Label | Vector | Origin |
|-------|--------|--------|
| v₀ | e₈ | Global Cayley-Dickson doubling scalar |
| v₁ | e_P | Fano Pole — single fixed point of the S₃ action |
| v₂ | e_{L₁} + e_{L₂} + e_{L₃} | Symmetric sum over Borromean-strand orbit |
| v₃ | e_{T₁} + e_{T₂} + e_{T₃} | Symmetric sum over Affine-coset orbit |

**Theorem 2.73.** Any linear combination of {v₀, v₁, v₂, v₃} is invariant under the S₃ permutation of the internal knot strands. These 4 vectors span the 4·triv subspace of the §2.72 decomposition.

*Proof.* By construction: v₀ is outside the S₃ action domain; v₁ is the fixed-point orbit; v₂ and v₃ are symmetric sums over the two transitive 3-orbits. Symmetric sums over transitive orbits of abelian-target group actions are trivially-transforming by standard representation theory. The dimension count matches: 4 = dim(4·triv) ✓. ∎

**Register 2 status is unconditional.** The GL(3,2) derivation is exact finite geometry with no approximation, no free parameters, and no physical input. The S₃ identification is forced, not chosen.

#### Part II — Physical Mapping: Structural Origin of the Relativistic 4-Vector (R3)

Because the internal Borromean strands share identical algebraic mass charges (§2.70 rigidity), their S₃ permutation dynamics are mathematically confined to the 2·std subspace of U(L). An external observer interacting with the knot through the surrounding vacuum substrate can only couple to the invariant subspace — the 4·triv sector. The knot therefore presents as a 4-component macroscopic object.

The natural (1,3) signature assignment:

- **v₀ = e₈:** The Cayley-Dickson doubling scalar bridging the first and second octonion copies. Structurally exterior to the Fano geometry; candidate for the scalar / time-like component.
- **v₁, v₂, v₃:** Constructed from purely imaginary Fano-plane units. Candidates for the 3 spatial components.

**This is a Register 3 structural analogy.** The identification of v₀ with "time" and {v₁, v₂, v₃} with "space" is motivated by the algebraic separation between the CD-scalar and the Fano imaginary units. It is not derived.

**Explicit promotion gates (both required for R2 promotion of the physical mapping):**

- **Gate A — Coarse-graining:** A formal density-matrix projection operator or explicit trace over the 2·std subspace is required, showing that the reduced state on the 4·triv sector is the physically accessible description. Dimension counting does not substitute for the projection map.
- **Gate B — Lorentz signature:** The (−+++) relative minus sign of the Minkowski metric must be derived from the sedenion non-associative or exchange algebra. It does not follow from the 1+3 orbit-count structure alone; a purely combinatorial (1,3) count could equally describe Euclidean ℝ⁴.

*Neither gate constitutes an Eddington Maneuver risk provided the R3 label is maintained and neither physical identification is cited as a derived result pending gate closure.*

### §2.82 The Borromean Enclosing-Sphere Ratio Does Not Yield R/r = 4 (Branch (a) of OP-2.25.2 Closed-Negative)

**Title:** Canonical Brunnian Conformations Do Not Produce an Enclosing-Sphere-to-Tube-Radius Ratio of 4.
**Status:** R2 computed negative result (promoted to the audit trail) + R3 provenance observation (filed, not for promotion). Closes branch (a) of the OP-2.25.2 attack vector. Cluster F (Borromean baryon thread); filed as a same-session companion to the PSL-nesting R3 entry (`ledger_entry_psl_nesting_closure_stratification_r3.md`, pending its own fold-in [resolved V4.19: filed as §2.83]), which staged the two-branch attack and directed effort to the Euclidean R = 4r question. Two Eddington flags active (Part III).
**Register:** R2 (Parts I–II, computed); R3 (Part IV pivot + observation).
**Eddington watch:** ACTIVE — two flags (Part III); both travel with any promotion of a sub-claim.

**Numbering rationale.** §2.82 is the next available §2.x slot after §2.81; filed in Cluster F at the cluster tail (after the §2.70–§2.73 block, leaving that block's summary intact), continuing the §2.30 three-strand / Borromean thread, parallel to the §2.80/§2.81 appends at the Cluster L tail.

#### Part I — Setup and the Round-Circle Exclusion (R1 background)

- **r** = tube radius (link thickness / normal injectivity radius); **R** = radius of the enclosing sphere of the whole link (tube surfaces). Physical identification under test (R3): R ↔ proton charge radius r_p; r ↔ proton reduced Compton wavelength λ̄_p, with the empirical near-coincidence **r_p/λ̄_p = 4.0008** (r_p ≈ 0.8414 fm, λ̄_p ≈ 0.21031 fm) as the target value.
- Round-circle idealizations are excluded a priori: the Borromean rings cannot be realized by three geometric circles (Freedman & Skora, *Strange actions of groups on spheres*, J. Diff. Geom. 25 (1987) 75–98; alt. proof Lindström & Zetterström, Amer. Math. Monthly 98 (1991) 340–341). Any R = 4r derived from a round-circle tangency model describes a configuration that is not topologically Borromean and is inadmissible. The door on round-circle idealizations is officially closed.

#### Part II — The Two Canonical Brunnian Conformations (R2, computed)

| Realization | enclosing surface | R/r |
|---|---|---|
| Tight (CFKSW four-arc) | tube surfaces | √7 + 2 ≈ 4.646 (16% high) |
| Tight (CFKSW four-arc) | centerline circumsphere | √7 + 1 ≈ 3.646 (9% low) |
| Golden ellipse (a/b = φ) | tube surfaces | 2φ + 3 ≈ 6.236 (56% high) |
| *(physical target)* | r_p/λ̄_p | 4.0008 |

- **Golden-ellipse realization** (three congruent ellipses, semi-axes a = φ, b = 1, in perpendicular planes, oriented cyclically — the icosahedral a/b = φ): thickness is set by inter-component spacing (on-axis gap φ − 1 = 1/φ; the curvature reach b²/a = 1/φ is not binding), so r = 1/(2φ), R = a + r, giving R/r = 2φ + 3 ≈ 6.236. Overshoots by ~56%; rejected.
- **Tight (CFKSW) conformation**, four-arc piecewise-circular model (arcs of radius-2 circles centered at the vertices of a rhombus of side 4 whose major diagonal exceeds the minor by 4; half-diagonals √7 ± 1; within 0.1% in length of the true ropelength minimizer, Cantarella–Fu–Kusner–Sullivan–Wrinkle, *Criticality for the Gehring link problem*, Geom. Topol. 10 (2006) 2055–2115). With unit-thickness tubes the link sits inside a sphere of radius √7 + 2 and clears a central ball of radius √7 − 2 (both values independently attested in the literature). Tube-surface ratio √7 + 2 ≈ 4.646 (16% high); centerline-circumsphere ratio √7 + 1 ≈ 3.646 (9% low).

**Verdict.** Combined with the prior-session exclusion of the hyperbolic (2,3,7) triangle ratio (≈ 5.37; companion PSL-nesting entry, `rosetta_stone_arxiv_v1.md`), all three canonical geometric ratios miss 4 — 5.37 (hyperbolic), 4.65 (Euclidean tight), 6.24 (golden ellipse). Ideal knot theory does not on its own deliver r_p/λ̄_p = 4. **Branch (a) of OP-2.25.2 is closed-negative.**

#### Part III — Two Eddington Flags (ACTIVE)

1. **The bracketing is a trap.** 4 lies strictly between √7 + 1 (3.646) and √7 + 2 (4.646). Choosing an intermediate enclosing surface — "the centerline plus 0.354 of the tube" — engineered to land on 4 is post-hoc selection of the success criterion, an Eddington maneuver, and is rejected. The statement of record: no pre-registered, independently motivated definition of the enclosing sphere yields 4.
2. **The √7 is not the F₇ prime.** The tight geometry genuinely contains √7 (enclosing sphere √7 + 2, central ball √7 − 2, half-diagonals √7 ± 1). This is a consequence of plain Euclidean rhombus geometry: side 4 with major diagonal exceeding minor by 4 gives (B + 2)² + B² = 16 ⟹ **B² + 2B − 6 = 0 ⟹ B = √7 − 1**. The 7 here is 1 + 6, an artifact of the unit-tube clearance arithmetic, with no established connection to the prime 7 of F₇ or to the order-7 holonomy of PSL(2,7). **It is strictly forbidden to conflate this √7 with the F₇ finite-field prime of the PSL(2,7) symmetry.** Reading it as "the order-7 structure appearing in the proton geometry" is vocabulary substitution and is rejected.

#### Part IV — Pivot to Branch (b) (R3)

Since pure ideal knot theory fails to produce r_p/λ̄_p = 4, any future physical derivation must rest on **branch (b)**: SQT's order-7 cone holonomy, acting on the Borromean tube configuration *under tension*, must **select** a non-canonical conformation whose enclosing-sphere-to-tube ratio is exactly 4. The burden of branch (b):

1. Specify the constrained variational problem — the conformation is no longer a free ropelength minimizer but a minimizer subject to the P¹(2,3,7) orbifold holonomy constraint.
2. Identify which of the 5 constrained degrees of freedom (9 → 5 after three cone-holonomy constraints plus Gauss–Bonnet, per the companion entry's orbifold count) is fixed by the order-7 cone holonomy.
3. Show that this constraint moves the enclosing ratio from the canonical √7 + 2 ≈ 4.646 to exactly 4 — i.e. forces the required ~16% shrink along the binding direction, the shrink factor being forced, not fitted.

Until (1)–(3) are discharged, R = 4r remains an unproved target, and the physical identification R ↔ r_p, r ↔ λ̄_p remains a motivated conjecture, not a derivation. Branch (b) is the sole surviving route.

#### Part I — The Exploratory Idea (as stated, preserved verbatim)

*User framing (verbatim intent):* Could constructing nested PSL groups — PSL(2,3) and PSL(2,5) acting as lower projections — be the route to proving the Borromean circumscription bound R = 4r from first principles? The quarks and perhaps fermions generally are the lower projections. Bosons ride the lattice wave-like. The electron is the stable closure that rides that wave. Point particles are unstable.

Preserved unedited so the original shape of the intuition is on record.

#### Part II — What the Group Theory Says (R1 facts; maximal-subgroup table corrected)

The genuine descending chain internal to PSL(2,7) is

  Z₃ ⊂ A₄ ≅ PSL(2,3) ⊂ S₄ ⊂ PSL(2,7),  orders 3 ⊂ 12 ⊂ 24 ⊂ 168.

- **The literal tower fails.** PSL(2,5) ≅ A₅ has order 60, and 60 ∤ 168, so A₅ is not a subgroup of PSL(2,7); the tower PSL(2,3) ⊂ PSL(2,5) ⊂ PSL(2,7) does not exist as subgroup inclusions. The intuition's literal form is refuted.
- **A₄ ≅ PSL(2,3)** is a genuine accidental isomorphism (both order 12), and it sits in the chain at the quark level.
- **Maximal subgroups (corrected):** two conjugacy classes of S₄ (order 24, fused by the outer automorphism) and F₂₁ = Z₇⋊Z₃ (order 21). D₄ (order 8) is the Sylow-2 and lies inside S₄ — a layer *within* S₄, not a rung of the maximal chain.
- **Physical reading of the chain (R2, from §2.43):** the orientation bifurcation (two PSL(2,7)-conjugacy orbits of S₄ subgroups) is a PSL(2,7)-level property; every step below S₄ is single-orbit. PSL(2,7) level = vacuum geometry / the two cones (outer automorphism connects them); S₄ level = the cone is entered, orientation fixed, order-4 elements first appear; A₄ ≅ PSL(2,3) level = the 3+1 structure where the quarks sit (up-quark stabilizer order 3 = line stabilizer in PG(2,2); down-quark stabilizer order 9 = amphicheiral figure-eight); Z₃ level = minimal cyclic closure. The Borromean F₇* stabilizer (order 6) is the multiplicative group of F₇, not a subgroup in this chain — it acts transversally, on Fano triangles.

#### Part III — Boson/Fermion Split and "Point Particles Are Unstable" (prior content)

The intuition's boson/fermion clause is already the framework's claim: bosons are propagating ΔS modes (photon = longitudinal ΔS wave, graviton = transverse ΔS wave — not closures); fermions are stable winding closures (electron = asymmetric (7,19) winding, a closure on the torus per Rule 17; proton = Borromean 3-link satisfying the full Fano-triangle condition). Consistent with the intuition; no new formal content added.

#### Part IV — What This Entry Contributes (R2-candidate)

The accidental isomorphism A₄ ≅ PSL(2,3) means the subgroup chain already contains a PSL-type group at the quark level, without imposing it. The quark stabilizers (order 3, order 9) live in exactly the chain level where PSL(2,3) ≅ A₄ sits. #### Part V — The OP.1 Orbifold Attack Vector (superseded/sharpened by §2.82)

The PSL nesting is not the load-bearing path to R = 4r; the group structure is already complete for the proton mass calculation. What is missing is a geometric lemma about the P¹(2,3,7) orbifold: three cone points with angles 2π/2, 2π/3, 2π/7; the Borromean tube configuration has 9 DOF before constraint; the orbifold imposes three cone-point holonomy constraints plus one Gauss–Bonnet closure, reducing 9 → 5. The orbifold / order-7-holonomy lemma (branch (b)) is therefore the sole surviving load-bearing route; its three-part burden is stated in §2.82 Part IV.

The PSL-nesting intuition: correctly identifies that the subgroup chain stratifies degrees of closure; contains a real accidental isomorphism (A₄ ≅ PSL(2,3)) already in the framework; does not provide a new derivation path for R = 4r; is consistent with existing framework content. ### §2.87.A Addendum — The ℂ⊗𝕆⊗ℍ Apparatus, the Distinct-4 Obstruction, and the Sharpening of Gate 2a

**Register.** R1 (the distinct-4 obstruction — two independent self-verifying proofs) + R2 (the ℂ⊗𝕆⊗ℍ tensor-product resolution; the convergence refinement; the substrate dictionary) + R3 (the spin-isospin locking postulate; the single-σ₄ unification fork, pre-registered and falsified). This subsection **refines the *reading* of §2.87's "four-4 convergence"** and discharges the §2.85 distinct-4 audit; it **retracts no §2.87 algebra result**.

**The distinct-4 obstruction (R1 — headline, two independent proofs).** No 4-dimensional space σ₄ can be at once a spin-3/2 module (irreducible under a spin-SU(2)) and a color 3 ⊕ 1 module (under a commuting SU(3)_color). *Proof 1 — finite, octahedral character (`gate2a_color_spin_transversality.py`):* on 2O (48 unit quaternions, closure verified), χ_{3/2}(q) = 2cos 3φ + 2cos φ gives χ(1) = 4, χ(−1) = −4 (central ↦ −Id, genuine spinor), ⟨χ, χ⟩ = 1 (irreducible), and **⟨χ_{3/2}, triv⟩ = 0** — σ₄|_{2O} has **no 2O-invariant line**; Furey's color-4 = 3 ⊕ 1 has, by construction, exactly one SU(3)-invariant line (the lepton singlet); the two are incompatible, equivalently C_{SU(4)}(SU(3)) = U(1) and 2O (order 48, non-abelian) ⊄ U(1). *Proof 2 — continuous, Schur + arithmetic (`gate2a_commutant_check.py`):* the commutant of the spin-3/2 SU(2) in M₄(ℂ) is **1-dimensional** (scalars — Schur); an embedded color-SU(3) does **not** commute (max commutator 2.0); and **3 ∤ 4**, so a 4 cannot host a (spin) ⊗ (color-triplet). A quark has a definite spin **and** a definite color at one instant, so those observables commute, so they live on **different commuting factors** — the same σ₄ cannot host both. This is the §2.85 distinct-4 audit, now proven two ways.

**The resolution: one apparatus = ℂ⊗𝕆⊗ℍ (R2).** "One baryon, one Clifford apparatus" stands — the apparatus is simply **larger than Cℓ(6)**. In the Furey–Gresnigt program the full algebra is **ℂ⊗𝕆⊗ℍ ≅ (ℂ⊗𝕆) ⊗ (ℂ⊗ℍ)**, a tensor product of commuting factors: **ℂ⊗𝕆 ≅ Cℓ(6)** is the **color/internal** factor (SU(3)_color = the G₂-stabilizer of a unit; spinor ideal 4 ⊕ 4̄ = one generation; **Furey's "4" = 3_quark ⊕ 1_lepton lives here**), and **ℂ⊗ℍ ≅ Cℓ(2)** is the **spin/isospin/Lorentz** factor (the SU(2) and the link to Spin(1,3); **the baryon's spin-3/2 SU(2) lives here**). The factors commute, so a state carries a definite color **and** a definite spin — exactly as physics requires and as the obstruction demands. **Cℓ(6) is the color sub-apparatus**; §2.87's "σ₄|_{2O} = spin-3/2" borrows the color factor's σ₄ for a spin role it does not carry.
