### §2.74 Császár/Szilassi Duality as Anchor/Circulation Identity

**Date filed:** May 25, 2026 (V4.4 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 2 (algebraic invariance under duality — unconditional) / Register 3 (physical identification of load tax ↔ vertex picture and crossing tax ↔ face picture — supported by structural pattern, not yet derived from first principles)
**Cluster:** L (Fano-Line Structure on Sedenion ZD Kernels)
**Cross-references:** §2.29 Theorem 4 (Császár-Szilassi factorization 84 = 21 × 4); §2.55 (Fano-line co-line kernel structure); §2.68 (Moreno-quadruple / K₇,₇ − M unification); §4.10 (top-quark-as-anchor; load tax / crossing tax distinction); Gauge Group paper v5 (Császár automorphism group / PSL(2,7)).
**Provenance:** `sedenion_yb_pair_search.py`, `sedenion_braid_rep.py`, `sedenion_braid_rep_L15.py`, `sedenion_braid_rep_orbit.py` (all May 25, 2026 session; F_911 working field).

#### Part I — Statement (R2)

The Császár and Szilassi polyhedra are combinatorial Poincaré duals on the torus T². They carry the **same** PSL(2,7) / octonion / sedenion algebraic structure but realize it through dual geometric primitives:

| Császár (vertex-based) | Szilassi (face-based) |
|------------------------|------------------------|
| 7 vertices             | 7 hexagonal faces      |
| 14 triangular faces    | 14 vertices            |
| 21 edges               | 21 edges               |
| Algebra basis = vertex set | Algebra basis = face set |
| Anchor points          | Circulation loops      |
| 0-cell                 | 2-cell                 |
| Adjacency-at-a-point   | Boundary-around-a-loop |
| Star of edges          | Cycle of edges         |
| Pointwise interaction  | Holonomy / flux        |

The algebra itself — multiplication table, automorphism group PSL(2,7), Cayley-Dickson lift to octonions and sedenions, the 42 Yang-Baxter pairs in the sedenion zero-divisor structure (May 25 finding) — is **invariant under the duality.** What changes is the interpretation of basis elements as *things at points* versus *things around loops*.

#### Part II — Why the Algebra Is Invariant (R2 — Unconditional)

The Cayley-Dickson construction depends only on the multiplication table at each doubling level, not on the geometric realization of the basis. Both Császár and Szilassi share:

1. The same 1-skeleton structure. Each touches/connects to 6 others among its 7 primary elements: 7-vertex with vertex-degree 6 for Császár; 7-face with face-adjacency 6 for Szilassi.
2. The same automorphism group action on the 7-element basis. PSL(2,7) acts equivalently on Császár vertices and Szilassi faces.
3. The same lift to the Fano plane — the imaginary octonion multiplication structure — via the standard vertex-Fano (Császár) or face-Fano (Szilassi) correspondence.

Consequently the sedenion algebra over either basis, and the 42-member Yang-Baxter family identified by the octad-straddle selection rule in the May 25 session, are identical objects.

#### Part III — What the Duality DOES Distinguish (R2)

The duality is not trivial. It exchanges anchor points ↔ circulation loops, 0-cells ↔ 2-cells, adjacency ↔ boundary, stars ↔ cycles, pointwise interaction ↔ holonomy/flux. Any construction sensitive to this distinction — orientation, boundary operators, holonomy phases, oriented integrals — will produce different geometric objects on the two duals, even though the underlying algebra agrees.

#### Part IV — Physical Mapping: Load Tax ↔ Vertex, Crossing Tax ↔ Face (R3)

This is the algebraic face of the anchor/circulation duality already present in the framework via the top-quark-as-anchor reframing (§4.10). That entry distinguished a **load tax** (paid by anchor points) from a **crossing tax** (paid by line-crossings/braids). §2.74 identifies these as two readings of one algebra:

- **Anchor / load tax** lives natively in the **vertex** picture (Császár): structural cost of holding the network open at a point.
- **Crossing / braid tax** lives natively in the **face** picture (Szilassi): structural cost paid along the boundary of a circulation cell when its loop is braided with another.

This is consistent with the May 25 Yang-Baxter finding. The 42 YB pairs are characterized by the **octad-straddle pattern** — index pairs crossing the Cayley-Dickson seam between octonion octad {1..7} and doubled octad {8..15}. Read through Császár: pairs where an interior anchor couples to an exterior anchor across the seam. Read through Szilassi: loops whose circulations cross the topological torus handle and pick up non-trivial braid phase. These are the same algebraic objects. The duality is the unifying frame.

**Register 3 fencing.** The physical identification of "load tax = vertex picture, crossing tax = face picture" is currently R2-supported and R3-derived. The algebraic invariance is unconditional; the physical mapping is motivated by structural pattern but not derived from a Lagrangian or action principle.

#### Part V — What This Entry Does NOT Claim

- Does **not** claim that Szilassi has a *different* sedenion algebra from Császár. The question was asked and the answer is no. (This is the primary closure: it rules out a previously-suggested route to a "second algebra.")
- Does **not** claim that the anchor/circulation duality is fully formalized at R1. The algebraic invariance is, but the physical identification of "load tax = vertex picture, crossing tax = face picture" is R2 / R3 — supported by the structural pattern but not yet derived from first principles.
- Does **not** claim that all framework dualities collapse to this one. Other dualities (unknot/Clifford-torus per Rule 17, inside/outside per the throat-origin paper) operate at different layers and should not be conflated.

#### Part VI — Open Questions Logged

1. **PSL(2,7) orbit decomposition of the 42-member YB family.** Does the 42-pair family decompose into PSL(2,7) orbits? If yes, how many orbits and of what sizes? Direct computation; tools in place via `subgroup_chain.py` and `csaszar_algebra.py`. *OQ1 CLOSED (May 26, 2026, V4.5): See §2.75. The natural CD-respecting lift of PSL(2,7) to a permutation action on sedenion indices {1..15} does NOT preserve the 42-pair set 𝒴 — 147 of 168 elements of PSL(2,7) take some YB pair to a non-YB pair. The maximal preserving subgroup is F₂₁ = N_{PSL(2,7)}(Sylow-7) ≅ ℤ₇ ⋊ ℤ₃ (the Singer-cycle normalizer / Frobenius group of order 21; one of the three maximal subgroup conjugacy classes of PSL(2,7) per Paper I / Dickson's classification). Under F₂₁, 𝒴 decomposes into exactly two regular orbits of size 21 (each with trivial stabilizer; each orbit is itself an F₂₁-torsor), distinguished by a quadratic-character handedness invariant on (ℤ/7)*. The two orbits are NOT PSL(2,7)-conjugate inside 𝒴: all 147 elements of PSL(2,7) \ F₂₁ take orbit 1 to a set NOT contained in 𝒴 (the negative result is decisive — no extension to a full PSL(2,7) action exists even when one is willing to permute the two F₂₁-orbits).*

2. **Frobenius-algebra refinement.** Does the boundary-operator distinction between Császár and Szilassi yield two different Frobenius-algebra refinements of the common sedenion structure, distinguishable by trace/cocycle data? *Logged, not promoted.*

3. **Hodge-style pairing.** Is there a natural Hodge-style pairing between Császár-vertex and Szilassi-face data that realizes the anchor/circulation duality as a non-degenerate bilinear form? *Logged, not promoted.*

#### Part VII — Audit Trail

- **Yang-Baxter pair enumeration:** `sedenion_yb_pair_search.py`, F_911, May 25, 2026 session. 42 hits, all with octad-straddle pattern.
- **Layer 1 braid-relation test:** `sedenion_braid_rep.py`. No pair satisfies the braid relation on the full 16-dim sedenion space.
- **Layer 1.5 defect-kernel analysis:** `sedenion_braid_rep_L15.py`. Three pairs (3,5), (3,7), (5,7) have braid-defect rank 8; all three generators have a+b=15 (index complementarity). *Forward pointer (V4.5, May 26, 2026): See §2.76 for the F₂₁-orbit membership of these three Layer 1.5 generators. The three generators (T_A, T_B, T_C) = (e₁+e₁₄, e₂+e₁₃, e₄+e₁₁) split 2-1 across the two size-21 F₂₁ orbits on the 49 octad-straddle twosets (T_A, T_C in one orbit; T_B in the other); none lies in the size-7 identity-doubled orbit. Of the three formal L1.5 operator-pairs (T_A,T_B), (T_A,T_C), (T_B,T_C), only (T_A, T_C) is itself a YB pair in 𝒴; the other two operator-pairs cross between the two F₂₁ twoset orbits and are not YB-coupled. §2.76 also records the stronger structural fact that the two F₂₁ YB orbits coincide exactly with the YB pairs internal to each size-21 F₂₁ twoset orbit (no YB pair crosses between the two TS orbits; no YB pair touches the identity-doubled orbit).*
- **Layer 1.5 orbit follow-up:** `sedenion_braid_rep_orbit.py`. ×4-mod-15 orbit pairing tested as a structural pattern.
- **Anchor reframing of top quark:** §4.10 of the SQT Master Ledger.

### §2.75 PSL(2,7) Does Not Act on the 42-Pair Yang-Baxter Family; F₂₁ Does, With Two Regular Orbits

**Date filed:** May 26, 2026 (V4.5 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 1 (direct exhaustive computation; all claims are finite group-theory facts verified by enumeration over the 168 elements of PSL(2,7))
**Cluster:** L (Fano-Line Structure on Sedenion ZD Kernels)
**Closes:** §2.74 Part VI Open Question 1.
**Cross-references:** §2.31 (sedenion ZD doubling-axis exclusion); §2.55 (Fano-line co-line kernel structure); §2.70 (F₇*-image rigidity companion); §2.71 (S₃ orbit structure 3+3+1 on PG(2,2)); §2.72 (§2.55 kernel S₃-decomposition); §2.74 (parent entry, Császár/Szilassi Duality); Paper I (PSL(2,7) Spectral Rigidity — F₂₁ = ℤ₇ ⋊ ℤ₃ as the order-21 maximal subgroup conjugacy class; Dickson's classification); Gauge Group paper v5 (PSL(2,7) as Császár automorphism group).
**Provenance:** `oq274_psl27_orbit_decomp.py`, `probe_preserving_subgroup.py`, `f21_orbit_analysis.py`, `chirality_invariant.py`, `orbit_final_checks.py` (all May 26, 2026).
**Inputs used:** The 42 YB pairs from `sedenion_yb_pair_search.py` (F_911, May 25, 2026, §2.74 audit trail); PSL(2,7) as GL(3,2) on F₂³ \ {0} from `oq1_orbit_schedule_bfs.py` (May 2026 session, verified order 168).

#### Part I — Statement (R1, two parts)

**Part A — Negative result.** The naïve CD-respecting lift of PSL(2,7) to a permutation action on sedenion indices {1..15}, defined by

  g · i        = g(i)        for i ∈ {1..7}
  g · (i + 8)  = g(i) + 8    for i ∈ {1..7}
  g · 8        = 8           (CD generator fixed)

does NOT preserve the 42-member Yang-Baxter pair family 𝒴 from §2.74 Part VII. Exactly 21 of the 168 elements of PSL(2,7) satisfy g · 𝒴 = 𝒴; the remaining 147 elements take some YB pair to a 2-subset of {1..15} that is not in 𝒴.

**Part B — Positive result.** The 21 preserving elements form a subgroup, identified as F₂₁ = N_{PSL(2,7)}(Sylow-7) ≅ ℤ₇ ⋊ ℤ₃ — the normalizer of any Sylow-7 subgroup of PSL(2,7), one of the three maximal subgroup conjugacy classes per Paper I / Dickson's classification. Under the F₂₁ action, 𝒴 decomposes into exactly **two regular orbits of size 21**, each with trivial stabilizer.

#### Part II — Setup (R1)

PSL(2,7) is realized as GL(3,2) acting on F₂³ \ {0} = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}. The natural CD-respecting lift of g ∈ PSL(2,7) to π_g ∈ Sym({1..15}) is as stated in Part I. 𝒴 is the 42-element set of unordered pairs of 2-subsets {(a₁, b₁), (a₂, b₂)} with a_i ∈ {1..7}, b_i ∈ {9..15}, computed by `sedenion_yb_pair_search.py`. F₂₁ is the unique-up-to-conjugacy maximal subgroup of PSL(2,7) of order 21; explicit generators are a Sylow-7 element σ (order 7) and an order-3 element τ normalizing ⟨σ⟩.

#### Part III — Derivation of the two regular orbits (R1)

**Step 1 (closure check).** Direct enumeration over PSL(2,7): for each of 168 elements g, compute π_g(𝒴) and test set-equality with 𝒴. Result: exactly 21 elements satisfy π_g(𝒴) = 𝒴.

**Step 2 (subgroup identification).** The 21 preserving elements form a subgroup of PSL(2,7) of order 21. Up to conjugacy, PSL(2,7) has a unique subgroup of order 21 — F₂₁ = ℤ₇ ⋊ ℤ₃ (Paper I / Dickson). Verify by inspecting the cycle structure of generators: a 7-cycle and an order-3 element acting on {1..7} via the standard Fano-plane / GL(3,2) generators of F₂₁.

**Step 3 (orbit count and sizes).** BFS on 𝒴 under the 21 lifted elements gives exactly two orbits, each of size 21. Sum: 42 ✓.

**Step 4 (regularity).** For both orbit representatives, the stabilizer in F₂₁ has order 1. By orbit-stabilizer, |orbit| × |stab| = 21 × 1 = 21 ✓. F₂₁ acts simply transitively on each orbit.

**Step 5 (faithfulness).** The kernel of the F₂₁ action on 𝒴 is trivial. F₂₁ ↪ Sym(𝒴) is an embedding.

**Step 6 (no extension to PSL(2,7)).** PSL(2,7) is simple, so the only homomorphism PSL(2,7) → S₂ (which would describe how an extended action permutes the two F₂₁-orbits) is trivial. Either PSL(2,7) preserves both orbits setwise, or PSL(2,7) does not act on 𝒴 at all. Direct check confirms the latter: all 147 elements of PSL(2,7) \ F₂₁ take orbit 1 to a set **not contained in 𝒴** (sets that intersect 𝒴 but include elements outside it).

#### Part IV — Orbit representatives

  Orbit 1 representative: {(4, 15), (6, 13)} ↔ axes (4, 7+8), (6, 5+8)
  Orbit 2 representative: {(1, 13), (3, 15)} ↔ axes (1, 5+8), (3, 7+8)

Both orbits exhaust all seven octonion axes; each axis appears in 12 half-twosets within each orbit (the balanced distribution noted in §2.74 Part VII).

#### Part V — Chirality invariant (handedness via quadratic character)

For each YB pair ((x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂)) with x_i ∈ {1..7}, y_i ∈ {9..15}, define s₁ = (y₁ − 8 − x₁) mod 7 and s₂ = (y₂ − 8 − x₂) mod 7. The pair (χ(s₁), χ(s₂)) — where χ is the quadratic character mod 7 (+1 on squares {1, 2, 4}, −1 on non-squares {3, 5, 6}) — is F₂₁-invariant up to multiset.

  Orbit 1 (label O_NEG, QNR-rich):
    {χ(s₁), χ(s₂)} = (−1, +1):  12 pairs
                     (−1, −1):   6 pairs
                     (+1, +1):   3 pairs
  Orbit 2 (label O_POS, QR-rich):
    {χ(s₁), χ(s₂)} = (−1, +1):  12 pairs
                     (+1, +1):   6 pairs
                     (−1, −1):   3 pairs

The mixed (−1, +1) count agrees; the homogeneous-sign counts are **swapped**. The two orbits are mirror images under the QR↔QNR involution of (ℤ/7)* / squares.

*[V4.16 forward pointer]* The two-regular-orbit decomposition and this quadratic-character chirality invariant are confirmed **over ℚ (characteristic 0, exact arithmetic)** by **§2.79** (comp_C): the F₂₁ symmetry of 𝒴 is a characteristic-0 fact, not an artifact of the finite-field (𝔽₉₁₁) model. §2.79 (comp_D2) further confirms that this F₂₁ is the **collineation** F₂₁ realized by 21 genuine sedenion automorphisms (not the affine label-group of §2.78-B).

#### Part VI — Why F₂₁ rather than full PSL(2,7) (R2)

The 42 YB pairs are defined by an algebraic (sedenion-multiplicative) condition, not by purely combinatorial Fano incidence. The combinatorial-only subgroup of PSL(2,7) preserving them is constrained to the part that **also** respects the octonion product structure (more precisely: the part whose lift via CD-respecting fixed-octad extension preserves the multiplication signs determining which sedenion products vanish). That intersection is F₂₁:

- The Sylow-7 (Singer cycle) generates "rotation by one step in the cyclic order of octonion units" — a genuine octonion-algebra automorphism via the seven-fold cyclic symmetry of the standard Fano-plane octonion multiplication table.
- The order-3 normalizer is the Frobenius-style automorphism of F₇ acting on (ℤ/7)* / {1, 2, 4} (the cube subgroup), permuting quadratic residues among themselves and quadratic non-residues among themselves.
- The involutions and order-4 elements in PSL(2,7) \ F₂₁ are Fano-plane symmetries that do not respect the octonion sign rules and therefore do not lift to algebra automorphisms.

Aut(𝕆) ≅ G₂, not PSL(2,7); F₂₁ is the largest part of PSL(2,7) that sits inside the relevant automorphism intersection.

#### Part VII — What this entry does NOT claim

- Does NOT claim F₂₁ is the FULL automorphism group of 𝒴 inside Sym({1..15}). The full sedenion-respecting symmetry group (allowing signed permutations and/or non-octad-fixing automorphisms) is strictly larger; what is claimed is that **inside PSL(2,7)** the maximal preserving subgroup is F₂₁.
- Does NOT claim the quadratic-character chirality is the only F₂₁-invariant distinguishing the orbits; other invariants may exist.
- Does NOT identify which orbit (if either) corresponds to a physically distinguished YB family. That mapping is downstream of the §2.74 Part IV R3 physical reading.
- Does NOT address §2.74 OQ2 (Frobenius-algebra refinement) or OQ3 (Hodge-style pairing).

> *Forward pointer (V4.15 fold-in, May 28, 2026):* §2.78 reconstructs the 42 twosets independently from the Cayley–Dickson table under the de Marrais "assessor" vocabulary (the same set as TS_O1 ∪ TS_O2) and confirms this entry's results from scratch. It records the complementary fact that the *underlying* PSL(2,7) acts **transitively** on the 42 twosets as a set (consistent with the negative result here, which concerns the finer YB-pairing relation 𝒴, not the set), and that the F₂₁ two-regular-orbit split is one of **eight** conjugate-Borel splits of the bare set — so §2.75/§2.76's TS_O1/TS_O2 partition is canonical precisely because it is the Borel pinned by 𝒴-preservation. See also §2.78 Part I-B for the disambiguation of the collineation F₂₁ used here from the affine label-group that does *not* lift to an octonion automorphism.

#### Part VIII — Open follow-ups raised

- **OP-2.74.1a.** Identify the full automorphism group of 𝒴 inside Sym({1..15}), allowing for signed permutations and/or non-octad-fixing automorphisms. Conjecture: strictly larger than F₂₁.
- **OP-2.74.1b.** Map the two F₂₁ orbits to a physical distinction in the CD-seam crossing orientation, if any. (Downstream of §2.74 Part IV R3.)
- **OP-2.74.1c.** Determine which F₂₁-orbit contains each of the three Layer 1.5 defect-rank-8 generators identified in §2.74 Part VII. *[Closed by §2.76 in same patch.]*
- **OP-2.75-CR (raised and CLOSED-with-result, May 26, 2026, V4.6):** Does the QR↔QNR involution that distinguishes the two F₂₁ orbits on 𝒴 extend to an involution on the spin representation of K₇'s symmetry group (PSL(2,7), spin cover SL(2,7))? Specifically, does it act as a "spin-flip" exchanging components of a fundamental spinor doublet? See **§2.77**. **Result:** The involution is genuinely outer of order 2 on F₂₁ and acts at the character level by swapping the two 3-dim irreps ρ_QR ↔ ρ_QNR. Lifted to SL(2,7), it is conjugation by s = diag(3, 5), an order-6 inner element. The spin-flip reading is **structurally refuted** because SL(2,7) admits no faithful 2-dimensional complex irrep (smallest genuine spin reps are 4-dimensional; see §2.D-FC for the strictly self-contained divisor-enumeration proof). The two 4-dim genuine spin irreps σ₄, σ₄' are F₂₁-Galois-twists of each other — a "rep-swap chirality" (Dirac-γ⁵-style) rather than an SU(2)-spin-component label. The Galois-twist relation is now Register 1 by direct induced-rep construction (May 27, 2026 audit).

#### Part IX — Methodological note (Eddington Maneuver discipline)

This entry has both a framework-disconfirming branch (Part A: PSL(2,7) does NOT act on 𝒴) and a framework-supportive branch (Part B: F₂₁ acts cleanly with orbit sizes 21 matching the subgroup order). Both branches are derived without consulting any experimental quantity; the result is a pure group-theoretic / combinatorial fact. Neither branch was reverse-engineered to fit a target.

### §2.76 Layer 1.5 Defect-Rank-8 Generators Are Split Between F₂₁ Twoset Orbits; The Two YB Orbits Coincide With Twoset-Orbit-Internal YB Pairings

**Date filed:** May 26, 2026 (V4.5 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 1 (direct exhaustive computation).
**Cluster:** L (Fano-Line Structure on Sedenion ZD Kernels)
**Closes:** OP-2.74.1c (raised in §2.75 Part VIII; closed in the same patch).
**Cross-references:** §2.31 (sedenion ZD doubling-axis exclusion — TS_IDOUB connection); §2.74 (parent entry, Layer 1.5 defect-rank-8 finding in Part VII); §2.75 (parent F₂₁ orbit structure on 42 YB pairs).
**Provenance:** `op_274_1c_l15_orbit_membership.py` (May 26, 2026).

#### Part I — Setup

The Layer 1.5 defect-rank-8 finding in §2.74 Part VII identified three sedenion-multiplication operator generators T_A = e₁ + e₁₄, T_B = e₂ + e₁₃, T_C = e₄ + e₁₁ with the index-complementarity property a + b = 15 for each operator. These three generators define three formal operator-pairs (T_A,T_B), (T_A,T_C), (T_B,T_C). The present entry resolves the F₂₁-orbit membership of these three generators (viewed as twosets in {1..15}) and the YB-pair membership of the three operator-pairs.

#### Part II — Twoset-level F₂₁ orbit decomposition (R1)

The 49 unordered twosets of the form {a, b+8} with a, b ∈ {1..7} — the "octad-straddle twosets" containing one index from each CD copy — decompose under the F₂₁ permutation action (inherited from the §2.75 lift) into exactly three orbits:

  TS_O1 (size 21): canonical representative {1, 14}; the orbit containing T_A.
  TS_O2 (size 21): canonical representative {2, 13}; the orbit containing T_B.
  TS_IDOUB (size 7): the identity-doubled orbit {(a, a+8) : a ∈ {1..7}}; the seven "diagonal" twosets where the octad-straddle pair is index-paired (i + 8) with its octonion source i.

Orbit sizes: 21 + 21 + 7 = 49 ✓.

> *Forward pointer (V4.15 fold-in, May 28, 2026):* The 42 = 21 + 21 non-diagonal twosets (TS_O1 ∪ TS_O2) are the de Marrais "assessors"; §2.78 reconstructs them and the seven box-kites from scratch, confirms TS_IDOUB = the §2.31 doubling-axis exclusion, and adds the box-kite octahedral layer (mutual-ZD components) absent elsewhere in the ledger, with the caution that the box-kite 3+3 splits and the A₄-coset 14-triple partition are non-canonical / routine on the bare set.

#### Part III — L1.5 generator orbit membership

- T_A = e₁ + e₁₄ = {1, 14} ∈ TS_O1.
- T_B = e₂ + e₁₃ = {2, 13} ∈ TS_O2.
- T_C = e₄ + e₁₁ = {4, 11} ∈ TS_O1 (verified by direct F₂₁ orbit BFS).

**L1.5 generators split 2-1 across the two size-21 F₂₁ twoset orbits**; none lies in TS_IDOUB. Of the three formal operator-pairs, **only (T_A, T_C) is itself a YB pair in 𝒴**; the other two — (T_A, T_B) and (T_B, T_C) — cross between TS_O1 and TS_O2 and are not YB-coupled.

#### Part IV — Alignment of YB orbits with twoset orbits (R1)

For every YB pair {(a₁, b₁), (a₂, b₂)} ∈ 𝒴, define its "component twosets" as t₁ = {a₁, b₁} and t₂ = {a₂, b₂}. Direct computation:

- **All 42 YB pairs have t₁ and t₂ in the same F₂₁ twoset orbit.** No YB pair crosses between TS_O1 and TS_O2. No YB pair touches TS_IDOUB.
- **YB orbit 1 (Part IV of §2.75) consists exactly of YB pairs whose two component twosets both lie in TS_O1.** YB orbit 2 consists exactly of YB pairs whose two component twosets both lie in TS_O2.

Equivalently: the two F₂₁ orbits on 𝒴 = the two F₂₁ twoset orbits, lifted to the YB-pair level via "both components from the same twoset orbit." The YB-orbit label is fully encoded in the TS-orbit label of any component twoset.

#### Part V — Structural observations (R2)

This part records the stronger structural fact going beyond what was recorded in §2.75 Part IV: **the YB-orbit decomposition is equivalent to the TS-orbit-of-component decomposition**. The chirality labeling introduced in §2.75 Part V is the per-twoset signed-skew χ lifted unchanged to YB pairs.

Three observations:

(a) **TS_IDOUB is the algebraic backbone.** The size-7 identity-doubled orbit {(a, a+8)} consists of exactly the twosets excluded from ZD participation by §2.31's doubling-axis exclusion. These never enter YB pairs. F₂₁ acts on them as the diagonal copy of the octonion-axis action.

(b) **L1.5 selection is chirality-uniform but TS-orbit-mixed.** The index-complementarity condition a + b = 15 picks out twosets of signed-skew χ = −1 (QNR) exclusively, but distributes them between TS_O1 and TS_O2 by a finer F₂₁-invariant not yet isolated.

(c) **(T_A, T_C) is uniquely YB-coupled.** Of the three L1.5 operator-pairs, only (T_A, T_C) is itself a YB pair in 𝒴. The other two are not YB-coupled. This asymmetry may signal that (T_A, T_C) is privileged among the three braid-defect-rank-8 candidates.

#### Part VI — What this entry does NOT claim

- Does NOT claim the L1.5 defect-rank-8 phenomenon has a physical interpretation. The L1.5 finding was a Layer 1.5 computational result; its meaning was not asserted in §2.74 beyond logging the rank-8 numerical fact.
- Does NOT identify the finer F₂₁-invariant that splits the six octad-straddle sum-15 twosets 3-3 between TS_O1 and TS_O2. The split is recorded but not characterized in closed form.
- Does NOT rule out a different computational invariant on YB pairs (not derived from the signed-skew χ) singling out the L1.5 pairs more cleanly.
- Does NOT address §2.74 OQ2, OQ3, or the §2.75 follow-ups OP-2.74.1a / OP-2.74.1b.

#### Part VII — Open follow-ups raised

- **OP-2.74.1c.i.** Characterize the finer F₂₁-invariant splitting the six octad-straddle sum-15 twosets 3-3 between TS_O1 and TS_O2 (split: (1,14), (4,11), (5,10) in TS_O1 vs (2,13), (3,12), (6,9) in TS_O2). Candidate: a multiplicative character of order 6 on (ℤ/7)* combined with a parity check.
- **OP-2.74.1c.ii.** Formalize the role of TS_IDOUB. These twosets are exactly the §2.31-excluded backbone elements. The F₂₁ orbit on them is the diagonal copy of the octonion-axis action and may be the algebraic substrate for the CD-seam crossings referenced in §2.74 Part IV.
- **OP-2.74.1c.iii.** Investigate the asymmetry that (T_A, T_C) is the unique L1.5 operator-pair that is also a YB pair in 𝒴. Test hypothesis: this pair is privileged among the three rank-8 candidates; the other two ((T_A, T_B), (T_B, T_C)) couple twosets across the TS-orbit boundary and may represent a structurally different phenomenon.

### §2.77 F₂₁ QR↔QNR Involution on SL(2,7) Spin Representations: Galois-Twist, Not Spin-Flip

**Date filed:** May 26, 2026 (V4.6 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 1 (representation-theoretic facts) + Register 2 (Galois-twist interpretation, now structurally proved by direct induced-rep computation).
**Cluster:** L (Fano-Line Structure on Sedenion ZD Kernels)
**Closes:** OP-2.75-CR (raised in §2.75 Part VIII; representation-theoretic follow-up on whether the QR↔QNR involution acts as a spin-flip). OP-2.77-σ4 (CLOSED-with-result May 27, 2026 by `induced_rep_check.py` + `part_iv_definitive.py`).
**Cross-references:** §2.75 (parent F₂₁ orbit structure on 𝒴); §2.76 (sibling — chirality propagation across structural levels); §2.D-FC (V4.6, R1, framework-constraint sibling — K₇ forces 4D spinors); §2.E-WD (V4.6, R3, downstream — Weyl doublet identification); Paper I (PSL(2,7) Spectral Rigidity, F₂₁ as Singer normalizer); `unaudited_conjecture_incomplete_closure_ferromagnetism.md` (parent question).
**Provenance:** `f21_chirality_spin.py`, `f21_spin_cleanup.py` (May 26, 2026 evening — initial computation and cleanup of F₂₁ irrep structure, SL(2,7) class enumeration, χ-lift); `induced_rep_check.py`, `part_iv_definitive.py` (May 27, 2026 — structural proof of Part IV Galois-twist relation by direct induced-representation computation).

#### Part I — Statement (R1)

The QR↔QNR involution on (ℤ/7)*, which distinguishes the two F₂₁ orbits on the 42-pair Yang-Baxter family 𝒴 per §2.75, extends as follows:

**(A) On F₂₁ itself:** χ_F21(a, b) = (3a mod 7, b) is a genuine group automorphism of F₂₁. χ_F21² equals conjugation by (0, 1) — inner. χ_F21 is therefore order 2 in Out(F₂₁) and a genuine outer automorphism modulo inner ones.

**(B) On F₂₁ irreducible representations:** F₂₁ has 5 irreps with dimensions (1, 1, 1, 3, 3). The three 1-dim irreps factor through F₂₁/ℤ₇ ≅ ℤ₃ and are χ-fixed. The two 3-dim irreps are induced from ℤ₇-characters χ_k(a) = ζ^(ka), with ρ_QR coming from the ℤ₃-orbit {1, 2, 4} = QR ⊂ (ℤ/7)* and ρ_QNR from the orbit {3, 5, 6} = QNR. **χ swaps the two 3-dim irreps** as a Galois-twist (verified at the character level on all 21 elements, both directions).

**(C) Lifted to SL(2,7):** Since |F₂₁| = 21 is odd, F₂₁ lifts uniquely to SL(2,7) as a literal subgroup (no projective-rep sign ambiguity). Explicit realization: u = [[1,1],[0,1]] of order 7, t = diag(4, 2) of order 3 with tut⁻¹ = u². The χ-involution is realized in SL(2,7) by conjugation by s = diag(3, 5), an order-6 inner element with s² = t² ∈ F₂₁. s ∈ N_singer \ F₂₁, where N_singer = ⟨u⟩ ⋊ ⟨diag(g, g⁻¹)⟩ has order 42.

**(D) On SL(2,7) spin representations:** SL(2,7) has 11 conjugacy classes (direct enumeration: class sizes [1, 1, 24, 24, 24, 24, 42, 42, 42, 56, 56], summing to 336). The 11 irrep dimensions split as {1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 8} factoring through PSL(2,7) (sum of squares 168) and {4, 4, 6, 6, 8} genuine spin irreps where −I acts as −1 (sum of squares 168). Total Σd² = 336, count 11 ✓. **SL(2,7) admits no faithful 2-dimensional complex irreducible representation** — the smallest genuine spin reps are 4-dimensional. (Cross-reference: §2.D-FC provides the strictly self-contained divisor-enumeration proof of this dimension split, replacing ATLAS lookup.)

#### Part II — Proof of Part B (Galois-twist on F₂₁ irreps)

The induced rep ρ_k of F₂₁ from a ℤ₇-character χ_k acts on a 3-dim space with basis {e_0, e_1, e_2} indexed by ℤ₃ cosets, via:

> ρ_k((a, b)) e_j = ζ^(k · ω^j · a) e_{(j+b) mod 3}

where ω = 2 (cube root of 1 mod 7) and ζ = exp(2πi/7).

This formula was verified as a genuine group homomorphism for both k = 1 (ρ_QR) and k = 3 (ρ_QNR) by exhaustive product-test on all 21² ordered pairs in F₂₁.

The character pullback χ_{ρ_QR} ∘ χ_F21 equals χ_{ρ_QNR} pointwise on all 21 elements of F₂₁ (verified by direct computation). By character-determinacy of irreps, ρ_QR ∘ χ_F21 ≅ ρ_QNR as F₂₁-representations.

#### Part III — Proof of Part D (No 2-dim faithful complex irrep)

The SL(2,7) conjugacy classes were enumerated by direct orbit computation over the 336-element group (all (a,b,c,d) ∈ (ℤ/7)⁴ with ad − bc = 1, under simultaneous conjugation). The result is 11 conjugacy classes with the stated sizes.

The dimension partition is then forced: by Schur's orthogonality, Σ d_i² = |G| = 336 with one d_i per irrep. The PSL(2,7) factor contributes 6 irreps with dimensions {1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 8} (sum of squares 168, well-known). The remaining 5 genuine spin irreps (those where −I → −1) must sum to 168 in squared dimensions. The strictly self-contained divisor-enumeration argument in §2.D-FC establishes that the unique 5-tuple of divisors of 336 with Σd² = 168 is {4, 4, 6, 6, 8}.

No 2 appears in either list. Therefore no faithful 2-dimensional complex irrep exists.

#### Part IV — Galois-twist structure of the 4-dim spin irreps (R2, now proved by direct construction)

The two 4-dim genuine spin irreps σ₄, σ₄' of SL(2,7), restricted to F₂₁, must decompose as sums of F₂₁ irreps (dimensions 1, 1, 1, 3, 3) summing to 4. The only non-degenerate decomposition is 4 = 3 + 1. Therefore:

> σ₄  |_F₂₁ ≅ ε_+ ⊕ ρ_QR
> σ₄' |_F₂₁ ≅ ε_− ⊕ ρ_QNR

for some 1-dim characters ε_±.

**Galois-twist relation (R2, now proved):** Since the χ-involution is realized inside SL(2,7) by conjugation by s ∈ SL(2,7), both σ₄ and σ₄' are individually s-invariant as SL(2,7)-representations. The χ-action *between* σ₄ and σ₄' is visible only at the F₂₁-restriction level, where it swaps the ρ_QR-summand into a ρ_QNR-summand. Equivalently:

> σ₄' ≅ σ₄ ∘ χ_F21  (as F₂₁-representations)

The two 4-dim spin irreps form a **χ-Galois-twist pair** at the F₂₁ level. They are not "swapped by an outer operator" in any way that acts internally on either irrep.

**Direct structural proof (May 27, 2026, `induced_rep_check.py` + `part_iv_definitive.py`):**

The induced representation Ind^{SL(2,7)}_{F₂₁}(ψ_0) (the F₂₁-trivial rep inflated to SL(2,7)) was constructed directly by counting fixed cosets of F₂₁ in SL(2,7) for each conjugacy class representative. Computation yields:

- dim(Ind) = [SL(2,7) : F₂₁] = 336 / 21 = 16 ✓
- χ_Ind on the 11 SL(2,7) classes (by order): {16, 0, 4, 0, 0, 2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0} (order 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 14, 14 respectively)
- ⟨χ_Ind, χ_Ind⟩_G = 4

The norm-squared equals 4, so by Frobenius reciprocity exactly 4 irreps of SL(2,7) contain ψ_0 in their F₂₁-restriction with multiplicity 1 each. Dimension count: 16 must be expressible as a sum of distinct irrep dimensions. The unique decomposition is:

> Ind^{SL(2,7)}_{F₂₁}(ψ_0)  ≅  triv (dim 1)  ⊕  σ₄ (dim 4)  ⊕  σ₄' (dim 4)  ⊕  Steinberg₇ (dim 7)

(1 + 4 + 4 + 7 = 16 ✓). Each summand has F₂₁-trivial summand multiplicity 1.

This decomposition combined with the central character constraint (−I acts as −1 on genuine spin irreps) determines σ₄'s character on every SL(2,7) class. On the F₂₁-visited classes (orders 1, 3, 7):

- σ₄(identity) = 4
- σ₄(order-3 class) = 1
- σ₄(QR order-7 class) = 1 + ζ_QR where ζ_QR = ζ + ζ² + ζ⁴ (Gaussian period over QR ⊂ (ℤ/7)*)
- σ₄(QNR order-7 class) = 1 + ζ_QNR where ζ_QNR = ζ³ + ζ⁵ + ζ⁶
- σ₄'(QR order-7 class) = 1 + ζ_QNR (Galois-twist of σ₄)
- σ₄'(QNR order-7 class) = 1 + ζ_QR

This matches **exactly** the values forced by σ₄|F₂₁ = ε_+ ⊕ ρ_QR (with ε_+ = ψ_0): the 1 from ψ_0 plus ζ_QR from ρ_QR on the QR class, and the swap on σ₄' as predicted by the Galois-twist. **Part IV is now Register 1 by direct construction**, not merely Register 2 motivated proof sketch. The earlier audit anomaly (non-integer multiplicities encountered in an intermediate attempt to read σ₄ from a borrowed character table) is resolved: the 3-dim PSL(2,7) irreps have character values (ζ_QR, ζ_QNR) on order-7 classes; the genuine 4-dim spin irreps have (1 + ζ_QR, 1 + ζ_QNR). The +1 offset distinguishing 3-dim from 4-dim is exactly the trivial-summand contribution that Part IV's decomposition predicts.

#### Part V — The Framework-Level Constraint

The non-existence of a faithful 2-dim complex irrep of SL(2,7) is **not** a contingent feature of the K₇ symmetry group; it is forced by the representation theory of SL(2, F_q) for q = 7. Anywhere SQT has informally invoked "K₇ spinor doublets," the actual native object is a 4-component spinor. This constraint is filed separately as §2.D-FC (Cluster D append) so that downstream framework arguments can cite it directly.

The constraint is structurally aligned with relativistic Dirac bispinor theory rather than non-relativistic Pauli doublet theory: a 4-component spinor with a discrete chirality label (left/right under a γ⁵-type involution) is exactly the natural object of relativistic spin-½. The F₂₁ Galois-twist label of Part IV is structurally analogous to γ⁵-chirality, though the physical identification awaits §2.E-WD.

**V4.7 update (May 27, 2026):** The Dirac-bispinor structural alignment claim above is **superseded** by the WD-1.a result (§2.E-WD closure section, V4.7). σ₄ harbors Cℓ(0,2) ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ (complexified quaternions), NOT Cℓ(1,3) Dirac. The F₂₁ Galois-twist is NOT structurally analogous to γ⁵-chirality — no γ⁵-type chirality operator on σ₄ exists at all (Schur on the irreducible σ₄ forces any commuting operator to scalar). The corrected structural alignment is **complexified quaternionic 1-spinor** (the natural carrier of Cℓ(0,2)), and the F₂₁ Galois-twist remains a real structural feature (proved R1 in V4.6 Part IV) but is now understood as a Galois-twist of the underlying quaternionic-2-spinor irrep pair (σ₄, σ₄'), not as a relativistic-chirality label. The R1 representation-theoretic content of Parts I–IV is preserved unchanged; only the Part V Register 3 interpretive language is corrected.

#### Part VI — Consequences for the Ferromagnetism Conjecture

Reframed Gate 1 Condition 1 of `unaudited_conjecture_incomplete_closure_ferromagnetism.md` (May 26 update) required showing that the F₂₁ L/R orbit label maps to electron spin direction. Two failure modes for the original spin-flip reading:

(a) **No fundamental doublet exists** in the K₇ spin representation structure, so "spin-flip on a doublet" is not a well-defined operation.

(b) **The χ-action is Galois-twist between irreps**, not an internal involution within a single rep — even if a doublet existed, χ would not act as a flip on it.

The Galois-twist reformulation (Path A in the conjecture update: "F₂₁ = Dirac γ⁵-chirality") preserves the F₂₁ chirality binary as a real physical-looking label but disconnects it from Hund's-rule spin maximization (which is an SU(2) Cartan eigenvalue Σ s_z statement, not a γ⁵-eigenvalue statement). A new mechanism for shell-level magnetic moment generation would be needed.

Alternatively (Path B): F₂₁ is not the right structure for ferromagnetism, and a different per-vortex property must be identified that *does* admit a 2-component representation.

Both paths are logged in §2.E-WD and the conjecture update; neither is pursued in this entry.

#### Part VII — What This Entry Does NOT Claim

- Does NOT claim that F₂₁-chirality is physically the Dirac γ⁵ chirality. The structural analogy is suggestive but the identification is an R3 question opened as §2.E-WD.
- Does NOT claim that the ferromagnetism conjecture can be rescued by Path A.
- Does NOT claim that the K₇ symmetry-group framework is committed to relativistic spin. §2.D-FC notes that the framework *natively* produces 4D spinor representations; whether those 4D objects carry standard Lorentz-bispinor structure or some other internal structure is open.

Any occurrence must either (a) be reframed in terms of 4D spinors per §2.D-FC, or (b) explicitly note that the framework feature in question does not use the K₇ symmetry-group spin reps but some other 2D structure (e.g., a quaternionic ℍ-fiber, which is a different mathematical object).

#### Methodological note

The result of this entry has both framework-disconfirming (no doublet) and framework-supportive (4D spinors are relativistic-Dirac-shaped) branches. Both branches were derived without consulting any experimental quantity. The computation began with the question of whether a specific conjecture's condition could be met, and produced a negative answer for that condition together with a structurally suggestive positive observation (4D bispinor naturalness). The negative answer is the load-bearing finding; the positive observation is logged as a new R3 exploration target rather than as evidence for a derivation that does not yet exist.

### §2.78 Assessor Twosets Are TS_O1 ∪ TS_O2; PSL(2,7) Acts Transitively on Them; the Affine "F₂₁" Does Not Lift to an Automorphism; the Single-Borel 21+21 Is Non-Canonical (Eight Borels)

**Date filed:** May 28, 2026 (V4.15 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 1 (orbit/partition facts by exhaustive enumeration, built from scratch from the Cayley–Dickson sedenion table in one fixed convention) + Register 2 (the structural reading of *what pins* the §2.76 split; the "no sedenion-specific content" assessment) + Register 3 (the methodological/Eddington meta-observation in Part V).
**Cluster:** L (Fano-Line Structure on Sedenion ZD Kernels)
**Relates to / confirms:** §2.74 (parent YB / Császár–Szilassi entry); **§2.75** (PSL(2,7) does not act on 𝒴; F₂₁ does, two regular orbits of 21); **§2.76** (the 49 octad-straddle twosets → TS_O1 + TS_O2 + TS_IDOUB under F₂₁); §2.77 (F₂₁ QR↔QNR involution on SL(2,7) spin reps).
**Cross-references:** §2.29 Theorem 4 (84 = 21 × 4; Moreno/Cawagas ownership of the 84-count); §2.31 (doubling-axis exclusion — the 7 excluded diagonal twosets = TS_IDOUB); §2.55 (Fano-line co-line kernel structure); §2.23 (PSL answers symmetry questions / Clifford answers capacity questions — the recurring register-confusion guard); Paper I (F₂₁ = ℤ₇ ⋊ ℤ₃ Singer-normalizer, Dickson classification); Gauge Group paper v5.
**External literature (newly attributed):** de Marrais 2000 (arXiv:math/0011260) — the "42 assessors," seven "box-kites," two-term-ZD framing; Moreno 1998 (*Bol. Soc. Mat. Mex.* (3) 4, 13–28) — the 84 normed two-term zero-divisors and G₂-homomorphic governance; Cawagas 2004 — independent box-kite derivation; Guterman–Zhilina and Chan–Đoković 2006 — refereed automorphism/subalgebra treatments.
**Provenance (May 28, 2026):** `correct_f21.py` (from-scratch CD sedenion table; 42 assessors and 7 box-kites built independently; order-168 automorphism group; all orbit computations), `check_f21_orbit_identity.py`, `test_automorphism.py` (Fano-line preservation test of the affine maps), `test_boxkite_invariance.py`.

#### Part I — Statement (R1 unless flagged)

This entry records a session that set out to claim a "novel F₂₁ orbit decomposition of the sedenion two-term zero-divisors cutting across the de Marrais two rows of 21." The audit dissolved the novelty on two independent grounds and, in doing so, **re-derived and confirmed the already-canonical §2.75 / §2.76 structure** while sharpening it.

**(A) Object identification (R1).** The 42 two-term zero-divisor "assessors" of de Marrais — pairs (eᵢ + e_j), i ∈ {1..7}, j ∈ {9..15}, j ≠ i+8 — are, under the reduced labeling (p,q) = (i−1, j−9) with p ≠ q, **exactly the 42 non-diagonal octad-straddle twosets of §2.76, i.e. TS_O1 ∪ TS_O2.** The seven excluded diagonal twosets {(a, a+8)} are §2.76's TS_IDOUB and §2.31's doubling-axis exclusion. Same 42-element set, two vocabularies.

**(B) Two distinct order-21 subgroups of S₇ (R1).** The abandoned draft conflated two non-interchangeable Frobenius groups of order 21:
- **The affine F₂₁** — the maps x ↦ ax+b on the reduced label field 𝔽₇ (a ∈ {1,2,4}, b ∈ 𝔽₇), applied coordinate-wise to (p,q). A subgroup of AGL(1,7). **It does not preserve the octonion Fano lines** (0 of its 21 elements preserve {123,145,167,246,257,347,356} under the standard CD table), hence it is **not** a subgroup of the octonion automorphism group and carries no algebraic meaning for the ZD structure.
- **The collineation F₂₁** — the Singer-cycle normalizer N_{PSL(2,7)}(Syl₇) ≅ ℤ₇ ⋊ ℤ₃ inside PSL(2,7) ≅ GL(3,2) acting on the seven Fano points. This is the F₂₁ of §2.75/§2.76. It preserves the Fano lines and lifts (with signs) to genuine octonion automorphisms.

**(C) Collineation lift and transitivity (R1).** Every one of the 168 Fano-collineations lifts to an octonion automorphism (sign system solvable for all 168; |P| = 168 = |PSL(2,7)|), and the canonical sedenion extension makes **PSL(2,7) act transitively on the 42 assessors and on the 7 box-kites.** This is the rigorous form of de Marrais's "seven isomorphic box-kites." It is *consistent* with §2.75: PSL(2,7) is transitive on the 42 twosets as a *set* but does **not** preserve the finer, sign-sensitive YB-pairing relation 𝒴, which is why §2.75 correctly found only F₂₁ ⊂ PSL(2,7) preserves 𝒴. The set is collineation-homogeneous; the YB relation on it is not.

**(D) The single-Borel 21+21 is non-canonical; §2.75/§2.76's split is the 𝒴-pinned one (R1 + R2).** The collineation F₂₁ (a Borel of PSL(2,7)) on the 42 assessors yields two regular orbits of 21 — **reproducing §2.76's TS_O1 / TS_O2.** But PSL(2,7) has **eight** conjugate Borel subgroups, verified here to give **eight distinct** 21+21 partitions (none equal to the de Marrais p<q / p>q rows; A/B-intersection signatures range over 9:12, 11:10, 13:8, …). **(R2)** So TS_O1/TS_O2 is canonical *only because §2.75 pins one specific Borel by the external criterion "preserves 𝒴."* Stripped of 𝒴, the bare 42-set admits no distinguished 21+21. This locates §2.76's content precisely: its canonicity is supplied by the sign-sensitivity of the YB condition (which breaks PSL(2,7) → F₂₁), not by anything intrinsic to the twosets.

**(E) Box-kite layer and the 14-triple object (R1 + R2).** The seven box-kites are the connected components of the mutual-zero-division graph on the 42 assessors; this graph is 4-regular (each box-kite an octahedron K_{2,2,2}). Three findings: (i) the F₂₁-induced 3+3 split of each box-kite is itself **Borel-dependent** (no common 3+3 across the eight Borels); (ii) "share an orbit under *all eight* Borels" is a genuine PSL(2,7)-invariant partition into **14 triples**; (iii) **(R2)** that 14-triple partition is the A₄-coset action of PSL(2,7) (triple-stabilizer of order 12 = A₄) — textbook PSL(2,7) subgroup combinatorics with no sedenion-specific content, registered to forestall a future "canonical 14-fold structure" overreach.

#### Part II — The draft-paper refutation (R1)

The draft's headline — "F₂₁ orbits cut across the de Marrais two rows of 21, hence novel" — fails twice: **(1) Wrong group.** Its F₂₁ was the affine label-group (Part I-B), not an octonion automorphism group; only an order-3 subgroup {id, (2,1), (4,3)} preserves the box-kites; the other 18 elements send some box-kite to a non-box-kite. The affine 21+21, its "7:14" transversality, and uniform "3+3" counts were relabeling artifacts — the failure mode the Prior Address Standard and Eddington flag exist to catch (21+21, 7:14, 3+3 fall out of any 42-set with any order-21 action and any 7-block partition). **(2) Not novel where real.** The genuine 21+21 is already §2.76's TS_O1/TS_O2 (V4.5), and the PSL(2,7)/F₂₁ governance of the ZD structure is de Marrais 2000 / Moreno 1998. A standalone paper would have duplicated canonical content *and* published literature without attribution. Net contribution: the affine-vs-collineation disambiguation, an independent from-scratch confirmation of §2.75/§2.76, and the non-canonicity result that sharpens where §2.76's canonicity comes from.

#### Part III — What this entry does NOT claim

- Does **not** retract or weaken §2.75 or §2.76 — both confirmed by independent reconstruction; the collineation-lift / F₂₁-maximality / two-regular-orbit results stand exactly as filed.
- Does **not** claim the box-kite octahedral layer is novel mathematics (de Marrais / Moreno / Cawagas structure, here re-expressed and connected to the twoset picture).
- Does **not** claim the 14-triple A₄-coset partition has physical or sedenion-specific content — generic PSL(2,7) subgroup combinatorics.
- Does **not** assert the affine F₂₁ is meaningless *as an abstract group* — only that, as label-affine maps, it is not an octonion automorphism group and is the wrong object for the ZD structure.

#### Part V — Methodological note (Eddington discipline, R3)

This session is a second-order data point for the V4.14 observation that walk-backs cluster around over-reaching claims while pure-math results hold. Here the pure-math results that held are §2.75 / §2.76 themselves — *confirmed*, not corrected. What got caught was a fresh over-reach (a "novel decomposition" on a misidentified group), caught by the same machinery: building from first principles, refusing to call a structure a symmetry before verifying it preserves the relevant relation, and checking canonicity rather than accepting the first suggestive 21+21. **Transferable lesson (logged for the index): in a 42-element set acted on by the 168-element PSL(2,7), divisibility manufactures suggestive numbers (21+21, 7:14, 3+3, 14×3) for almost any subgroup choice, each dissolving into non-canonicity or routine subgroup combinatorics under audit.** The object is small and classically understood; new content is unlikely to live in its orbit/box-kite combinatorics. The genuinely open candidate from this thread remains *outside* it — the Yang–Baxter / braid-representation structure of §2.74 (Layer 1.5, OP-2.74.1c.i/ii/iii), where the sign-sensitivity that breaks PSL(2,7) → F₂₁ actually carries the content. This is the §2.23 register guard in action: PSL(2,7) answers symmetry questions; the box-kite/assessor combinatorics are capacity-style bookkeeping.

### §2.79 The 42-Pair Yang–Baxter Set Through the Braid/Torsor Lens: Outer-Automorphism Stability of F₂₁, the Octad-Swap Is Non-Algebraic, and the Two Orbits Are Spectrally Degenerate (Split Only by the Singer Chirality Invariant)

**Date filed:** May 29, 2026 (V4.16 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 1 (all orbit/automorphism/torsor/spectral facts by exhaustive enumeration, computed two ways — over 𝔽₉₁₁ and over ℚ — from the Cayley–Dickson sedenion table in one fixed convention) + Register 2 (the reading of *what pins* the two-block partition; the "C₂ is non-algebraic" assessment; partial progress on OP-2.78.1/2) + Register 3 (one Eddington-guarded resonance with §2.77, explicitly not promoted).

Monthly* 116(8), 727–732 — PSL(2,7) ≅ GL(3,2); the point↔line duality φ = inverse-transpose is classical); ATLAS (Conway et al. 1985).

All import the integer / 𝔽₉₁₁ CD multiplication table from `sedenion_Fp.py`.

#### Part I — Statement (R1 unless flagged)

This entry is the immediate continuation of §2.78. Where §2.78 audited the 42-element set through the **de Marrais assessor** lens (the bare set and its box-kites), this session re-ran the audit through the **Yang–Baxter pair / braid-operator** lens (the relation 𝒴 of §2.74/§2.75 and the symmetric braid operator on it), examined the **outer-automorphism stability** of the symmetry group, and tested whether the F₂₁ × C₂ torsor admits a **canonical basepoint**. Every result reconfirms §2.75/§2.76/§2.78; two are new.

**(A) Outer-automorphism action on the subgroup lattice (R1; new).** On PSL(2,7) ≅ GL(3,2), the map φ(g) = (gᵀ)⁻¹ (inverse-transpose, the algebraic form of the Fano point↔line duality) is an automorphism of order 2 and is **outer** (it does not fix the two conjugacy classes of point-stabilizers, so it cannot be inner). φ **swaps** the two S₄ classes (point-stabilizer ↔ line-stabilizer) and **fixes** the F₂₁ (Singer-cycle-normalizer) class; every subgroup order with a unique class (C₂, C₃, C₄, V₄, S₃, C₇, D₄, A₄) is fixed by force. *Consequence for the YB story:* the symmetry group of 𝒴 — the collineation F₂₁ of §2.75 — is **stable under the full outer-automorphism group of PSL(2,7)**, i.e. it is duality-self-conjugate, whereas the two S₄'s are duality-partners. This is the computed form of the draft's "Claim 3.2," and it supplies a computed data point toward Paper I's Open Problem 4.5 (S₄ = Stab(point), S₄′ = Stab(line) exchanged by duality; F₂₁ = Stab(line)/Singer self-dual). **Not novel mathematics** — the point↔line duality is classical (Brown–Loehr 2009) — recorded as a confirmation and newly connected to the YB symmetry group's outer-stability.

**(B) The YB-set symmetry group is the collineation F₂₁, not PSL(2,7) (R1; confirms §2.75, refutes draft Claim 3.3).** The diagonal symmetry group G_diag of the 42 sedenion Yang–Baxter pairs (octad-straddling; e₈ absent from every index used) has **order 21** and equals the collineation F₂₁: G_diag ⊆ Aut(Fano) = PSL(2,7) holds, but Aut(Fano) ⊆ G_diag **fails** (G_diag ⊊ PSL(2,7), 21 < 168). On the 84-element two-term-ZD generator set, PSL(2,7) acts in a **single orbit** [84] (collineation-homogeneous, as in §2.78-C) while F₂₁ gives four orbits of 21; on the 42 **unordered** pairs F₂₁ gives **two** regular orbits of 21 (Part C). This refutes the draft's load-bearing "Claim 3.3" (G_diag = PSL(2,7)); the correct statement is **G_diag = collineation F₂₁**, exactly §2.75. Orbit sizes for the other subgroups (the two S₄'s, A₄, S₃, C₇) are recorded as routine bookkeeping with no sedenion-specific content (the §2.78 lesson).

**(C) The result is characteristic-0, not a finite-field artifact (R1; draft Claim 4.5a).** Recomputed over ℚ with exact integer/Fraction arithmetic (sedenion structure constants ∈ {−1,0,+1}, so the construction is defined over ℤ): 42 YB pairs, all octad-straddling; diagonal symmetry of order 21 with element-order multiset {1:1, 3:14, 7:6} = F₂₁ = C₇⋊C₃; the octad-swap ρ preserves 𝒴; F₂₁ orbit sizes on the 42 pairs = [21, 21]; ⟨F₂₁, ρ⟩ acts transitively (order-42 regular torsor). **Identical to the 𝔽₉₁₁ result.** This upgrades §2.75's facts from "verified over a mod-455 prime" to **characteristic-0 facts**.

**(D) F₂₁ × C₂ = (genuine automorphisms) × (non-algebraic seam swap) (R1; draft Claim 4.5c; sharpens §2.78).** The bare octad-swap ρ (eₖ ↔ ℓ·eₖ, i.e. index k ↔ 8+k for k=1..7, fixing e₀ and e₈) is **neither** an algebra automorphism (holds on only 46/256 basis products) **nor** an antiautomorphism (88/256); the four sign-variants merely swap those two counts (46/88 ↔ 88/46), none reaching 256/256. So ρ is **not** an (anti)automorphism — it is the Cayley–Dickson component-swap (p,q) ↦ (q,p), a combinatorial symmetry of the ZD/YB structure only. Separately, of the 168 unsigned Fano-line-preserving permutations, **exactly 21** are genuine sedenion automorphisms (nonabelian, orders {1:1, 3:14, 7:6} = F₂₁). Net: the YB symmetry **F₂₁ × C₂** factors as (the algebraic, automorphism-realized F₂₁) × (the non-algebraic seam-swap C₂). This is the algebraic confirmation of §2.78's collineation-F₂₁ identification and makes explicit which factor is and is not realized by the algebra.

**(E) The torsor has no canonical basepoint; the two orbits are spectrally degenerate, split only by the Singer chirality invariant (R1 computation + R2 reading; new; partial OP-2.78.1).** Under the full F₂₁ × C₂, the action on the 42 pairs is **free and transitive** (regular torsor): the maximum F₂₁-stabilizer over all 42 pairs is 1, and **0** pairs are fixed by ρ — so no single YB pair is distinguished by symmetry (no canonical origin; the torsor is affine). However, the two F₂₁ orbits form a canonical unordered 2-block partition, and the key new fact is *how* it is — and is not — detected:
- **Invisible to the braid spectrum.** The symmetric braid operator (A+B)|_V has the **identical** power-trace fingerprint (tr, tr², tr³, tr⁴) = **(0, 895, 0, 64)** on both orbits, constant within each orbit, and ρ carries an O₁ representative to a pair with the same spectrum. The two orbits are spectrally degenerate.
- **Visible only combinatorially.** The partition is tracked by the **Singer difference (fano − low) mod 7** — i.e. the §2.75 quadratic-character (QR↔QNR) chirality invariant — whose distribution over the grid points is {1:6, 2:4, 4:14, 5:10, 6:8}, with all 42 grid points {low, fano} lying on a Fano line.

**(R2) reading.** (i) This is partial progress on **OP-2.78.1/OP-2.78.2**: the canonical 2-block partition is the §2.75 chirality split, pinned by a *combinatorial* (Singer/Galois) datum and not by any spectral/representation invariant of the braid operator. *(V4.17: OP-2.78.1, OP-2.78.2, and OP-2.79.1 are now closed R1 in §2.80.)* (ii) It is mutually consistent with **§2.77** ("Galois twist, not spin flip"): there the two genuine spin irreps σ₄, σ₄′ are not separated by a representation-theoretic invariant, only by the QR↔QNR Galois twist; here the two YB orbits are not separated by the braid spectrum, only by the QR↔QNR Singer datum. The parallel is logged as a resonance, **not** an identification (see Part VI, OP-2.79.2, and the Eddington guard below).

### §2.81 Even-Term Parity of Clean Sedenion Zero Divisors: the Rank-12 Boundary Skin Recurs at n = 4 but Vanishes at Odd n; Prime-Class Independence (OP-2.25.2-V3 / V4 closure)

**Date filed:** May 29, 2026 (V4.17 fold-in)

#### Part I — V4: prime-class independence (R1)
The two-term cross-edge ZD boundary skin — 84 ZDs, each with rank(L_x) = 12 (4-D kernel), kernel basis four clean two-term cross-edge ZDs, and kernel pair-triple = the three Fano lines through a missing point m (§2.55 co-line structure) — is **identical** at p = 101, 103, 65537 (all p ≢ 1 mod 455) and at the q ≡ 1 mod 455 baselines (911, 2731). The structure is therefore **not an artifact of the q ≡ 1 mod 455 prime class** used by the crypto thread; it is a property of the integer Cayley–Dickson table reduced mod p (for p outside the small primes {5, 7, 13}). **OP-2.25.2-V4 closed (positive).**

(Verified at p = 911 and p = 103; identical.) ### §2.E-WD Weyl Doublet Identification: Mapping the Two 4D Genuine Spin Irreps of SL(2,7) to L/R Weyl Doublets of the Dirac Bispinor

**Date opened:** May 26, 2026 (V4.6 fold-in)
**Status:** Register 3 — Exploration target, banked. Do not promote without explicit construction.
**Cluster:** L (Fano-Line Structure on Sedenion ZD Kernels), tail append as R3 banked
**Mode:** Exploration only. No derivation claimed.
**Cross-references:** §2.77 (V4.6, parent — Galois-twist structure of σ₄, σ₄', now Register 1 by direct construction); §2.D-FC (V4.6, sibling — 4D spinor framework constraint); `unaudited_conjecture_incomplete_closure_ferromagnetism.md` (downstream consumer of any positive result here).

#### The Question

The standard Dirac bispinor on 4D Minkowski space decomposes under the Lorentz group SO(3,1) (or its double cover SL(2, ℂ)) into two 2-component Weyl spinors:

> ψ_Dirac = ψ_L ⊕ ψ_R

where ψ_L transforms in the (1/2, 0) irrep of SL(2, ℂ) and ψ_R in the (0, 1/2). The two are interchanged by the Dirac γ⁵ operator, which is the Lorentz-invariant chirality involution.

§2.77 (V4.6, R1) established that the K₇ symmetry group's spin double cover SL(2,7) admits two distinguished 4-dimensional genuine spin irreps σ₄, σ₄', related as F₂₁-Galois-twists of each other under the QR↔QNR involution. The Galois-twist label is structurally analogous to γ⁵-chirality.

**The R3 question:** Is there a natural identification of σ₄ ⊕ σ₄' with the Dirac bispinor decomposition ψ_L ⊕ ψ_R? Equivalently, is the F₂₁ Galois-twist involution mathematically conjugate to a γ⁵-type chirality operator on a Dirac bispinor?

#### Why this is an exploration target rather than a conjecture

The structural analogy is suggestive but not yet matched:

- **What matches:** Both are 4-dim spinors with a 2-fold chirality split; both have a discrete involution swapping the chirality labels; both treat the chirality as a representation-level label rather than a state-component label.

- **What does not yet match:** The Dirac bispinor's chirality split is under SL(2, ℂ) (the complexified Lorentz group), not SL(2,7). SL(2, ℂ) is a continuous Lie group of complex dimension 3; SL(2,7) is finite of order 336. The two are not group-theoretically conjugate in any obvious way. A correspondence between σ₄ ⊕ σ₄' and ψ_L ⊕ ψ_R would have to be of a structural-analogy nature (e.g., both arise from a similar group-theoretic skeleton) rather than a representation isomorphism.

#### The three sub-questions

A formal answer to the R3 target requires three layers of work, each load-bearing:

**WD-1: Group-theoretic embedding.** Does SL(2,7) embed in (or relate to) SL(2, ℂ) in a way that respects the chirality structure? Concretely: is there a homomorphism SL(2,7) → SL(2, ℂ) (or some natural extension) such that σ₄, σ₄' restrict from a Dirac-like bispinor rep, with the F₂₁ Galois-twist becoming the γ⁵ chirality?

**WD-2: Chirality operator identification.** Even without an embedding, is there a 4×4 matrix Γ on the σ₄ ⊕ σ₄' representation space such that (a) Γ² = I, (b) Γ has +I-eigenspace on σ₄ and −I-eigenspace on σ₄' (or vice versa), and (c) Γ commutes with the SL(2,7) action? If yes, Γ is the framework's intrinsic γ⁵, and §2.77 Part IV's Galois-twist becomes a Γ-eigenspace decomposition.

**WD-3: Physical mapping.** If WD-1 and/or WD-2 succeed, can the framework's 4D bispinor be identified with a physical Dirac bispinor (e.g., the electron's Dirac field) such that:
- The F₂₁-chirality of the per-vortex YB orbit assignment corresponds to electron γ⁵-chirality.
- Shell-level packing across the 2ℓ+1 orientation slots produces observable magnetic moments via a γ⁵-imbalance mechanism (Path A of the ferromagnetism conjecture's two paths).
- Or, if not, what other physical interpretation the K₇ bispinor carries.

#### Promotion gate to R2

Promotion of any part of §2.E-WD to R2 requires **at minimum** a derivation of WD-1 or WD-2 (Galois-twist = γ⁵ structurally) by explicit construction. WD-3 is downstream; it cannot be addressed without WD-1 or WD-2 first.

A negative result on WD-1 and WD-2 (i.e., showing that σ₄ ⊕ σ₄' is NOT naturally a Dirac bispinor) is also a legitimate closure of §2.E-WD. The exploration is genuinely open in both directions.

#### Standing constraints on this exploration

- **§2.D-FC compliance.** Any work under §2.E-WD must respect that K₇ does not have a 2-dim faithful spin rep. Approaches that informally introduce a 2D Pauli-doublet structure mid-derivation are immediately suspect.

- **§2.45-OPM Finding 1 compliance.** Any work under §2.E-WD must not cross the per-vortex / shell-filling scale boundary without an explicit bridge (per the lesson logged in the V4.6 ferromagnetism conjecture update).

- **Galois-twist character vs. γ⁵ character.** The F₂₁ Galois-twist swaps representations of a finite group; the γ⁵ chirality swaps representations of a continuous Lie group (the Lorentz group). A successful identification must address why these very different structural origins produce the same algebraic content.

#### What is NOT being claimed by opening this target

Opening §2.E-WD as an R3 exploration target does NOT mean the framework is committing to a relativistic Dirac picture for K₇. It is logging the question of whether such a picture is structurally available, with both positive and negative answers held open until explicit construction work is done.

#### V4.7 closure (May 27, 2026) — Negative result by explicit matrix construction

**Status promoted from R3 (exploration target, open) to R1 (closed with negative result by direct computation).**

**Provenance:** `sigma4_build_step1.py`, `sigma4_build_step2.py`, `sigma4_data.npz` (σ₄ basis); `clifford_hunt.py` (clique enumeration); `cl03_chirality_structure.py` (Schur check); `cl02_correction.py` (Cℓ(0,2) identification); `WD_1a_result_memo.md` (full prose write-up).

**Construction:** σ₄ was built as explicit 4×4 complex matrices via character projection from Ind^{SL(2,7)}_{F₂₁}(triv). The projection operator P_σ₄ = (4/336) Σ_g χ̄_σ₄(g) · ρ_Ind(g) was verified rank-4, idempotent to ~10⁻¹⁷; an orthonormal basis Q ∈ ℂ^{16×4} was extracted, giving σ₄(g) = Q† ρ_Ind(g) Q. Consistency checks pass to ~10⁻¹⁵: σ₄(e) = I₄, σ₄(−I) = −I₄, σ₄(u)⁷ = I₄, Tr(σ₄(u)) = 1 + ζ_QR matching Part IV's prediction exactly, homomorphism σ₄(g₁g₂) = σ₄(g₁)σ₄(g₂) verified on 20 random pairs.

**Γ-matrix hunt (WD-2):** For each of the 42 order-4 elements x ∈ SL(2,7) (all satisfying x² = −I), define Γ_x = −iσ₄(x). All 42 satisfy Γ_x² = +I₄ and Tr(Γ_x) = 0 — the right spectral signature for γ⁵-candidate operators. Exhaustive search across the 42 candidates:

| Anticommuting clique size | Count |
|---|---|
| 2 (pairs) | 168 |
| 3 (triples) | 112 |
| 4 (quadruples) | **0** |
| 5+ | 0 |

**Cℓ(0,3) collapse to Cℓ(0,2):** All 112 anticommuting triples satisfy Γ₁Γ₂Γ₃ = ±i·I₄ (scalar volume element), with the 112 split exactly 56/+iI and 56/−iI. The third generator is forced by the first two via Γ₃ = ±iΓ₁Γ₂, so these are not three independent Cℓ(0,3) generators but Cℓ(0,2) generator pairs with one derived element. Span dimension check confirms: span{I, Γ₁, Γ₂, Γ₁Γ₂} has complex rank 4 = M₂(ℂ); adding Γ₃, Γ₁Γ₃, Γ₂Γ₃, ω does not increase rank. The full algebra generated by the order-4 Γs has complex dimension 4, not 8 (Cℓ(0,3)) or 16 (Cℓ(1,3)).

**Null-space verification:** For an arbitrary 3-clique, the linear system requiring a 4×4 matrix M to anticommute with all three Γs has null space dimension **0** in the full 16-dim space of 4×4 matrices. No completion to a 4-clique exists, not just in σ₄ but in M₄(ℂ) entirely.

**Schur consistency:** The candidate volume operator ω = Γ₁Γ₂Γ₃ commutes with the full SL(2,7) action on σ₄ to ~10⁻¹⁵ (tested on u, t, s, and a random order-24 element). By Schur's lemma on the irreducible σ₄, ω must be scalar — which is exactly what direct computation shows (ω = ±i·I₄). The chirality decomposition that γ⁵ would provide is **structurally forbidden** by the irreducibility of σ₄ as an SL(2,7)-representation.

**Structural verdict:**

| Hypothesis | Required structure | Available in σ₄ |
|---|---|---|
| Cℓ(1,3) Dirac (signature 1,3) | 4 mutually anticommuting Γs | 0 quadruples |
| Cℓ(3,1) Dirac (signature 3,1) | 4 mutually anticommuting Γs | 0 quadruples |
| Cℓ(0,4) Euclidean | 4 mutually anticommuting +I | 0 quadruples |
| Cℓ(0,3) Pauli-like (independent) | 3 independent anticommuting +I | 0 (all triples have scalar ω) |
| **Cℓ(0,2) ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ ≅ M₂(ℂ)** | **2 mutually anticommuting +I** | **168 pairs ✓** |

**σ₄ does NOT natively harbor the Cℓ(1,3) Dirac Clifford algebra.** σ₄ harbors **Cℓ(0,2) ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ** (complexified quaternions, equivalent to the Pauli matrix algebra). σ₄ is structurally a complexified quaternionic 1-spinor (a 1-dim quaternionic space viewed as 2-dim over ℂ, doubled to act faithfully on ℂ⁴), NOT a Dirac 4-spinor.

**Sub-question outcomes:**

- **WD-1 (group-theoretic embedding):** Closed negatively. No SL(2,7) → SL(2,ℂ) embedding can make σ₄ ⊕ σ₄' a Dirac bispinor pair because σ₄ itself fails to carry the required Cℓ(1,3) anticommuting set.
- **WD-2 (chirality operator identification):** Closed negatively by Schur's lemma. No 4×4 matrix Γ on σ₄ with Γ² = I, Tr(Γ) = 0, and commuting with the SL(2,7) action exists; any such operator would be scalar by Schur, contradicting Tr = 0 (or Γ² = I if it were 0).
- **WD-3 (physical mapping):** Reformulated rather than answered. The physical comparison shifts from the Dirac electron field to non-relativistic Pauli-spinor / SU(2)-doublet structure, since σ₄ ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ matches the quaternionic structure that SU(2) ≅ unit quaternions naturally acts on. This reformulation is opened as §2.E-QQ.

**Path A of ferromagnetism conjecture (F₂₁ = γ⁵-chirality):** Structurally closed. No γ⁵ exists on σ₄ at all, so F₂₁ Galois-twist cannot be identified with γ⁵-chirality. The F₂₁ Galois-twist remains a real structural feature (Part IV R1) but is now understood as a Galois-twist between two quaternionic-1-spinor irreps, not as a relativistic-chirality label.

**Path B of ferromagnetism conjecture (alternative per-vortex carrier):** Reopened concretely. The complexified quaternionic structure of σ₄ might be the right substrate for SU(2)-spin-like behavior IF an SL(2,7) subgroup can be identified that acts on σ₄ as SU(2). This is the substance of §2.E-QQ.

**Promotion gate satisfied:** §2.E-WD's R2 promotion gate (per the original V4.6 entry) required derivation of WD-1 or WD-2 by explicit construction; a negative result was explicitly allowed as legitimate closure. WD-1.a delivers a definitive negative by explicit construction. The exploration target is closed.

#### Methodological note on V4.7 closure

The WD-1.a result is framework-disconfirming on the specific Dirac-bispinor hypothesis without consulting any experimental quantity. The construction worked entirely from §2.77 Part IV's induced-rep proof + the divisor-enumeration proof of §2.D-FC; no external character table or physics input was used. The negative result strengthens framework discipline by replacing an under-specified analogy (4D spinor "like Dirac") with a precise algebraic identification (4D spinor = complexified quaternionic 1-spinor = Cℓ(0,2)). The §2.D-FC R1 framework constraint is preserved unchanged; only its Register 3 interpretive language is sharpened.

#### The Question

§2.E-WD V4.7 closure established that σ₄ harbors Cℓ(0,2) ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ — the complexified quaternions. Given any pair (Γ_x, Γ_y) of anticommuting order-4 elements of SL(2,7), the σ₄-images σ₄(x), σ₄(y) generate a copy of the quaternion algebra acting on σ₄.

The natural physical-spinor object carrying a ℍ⊗ℂ structure is the **SU(2) doublet** — i.e., a 2-component complex spinor on which SU(2) ≅ unit quaternions acts faithfully. The Pauli matrices σ_x, σ_y, σ_z are the standard Cℓ(0,3) generators on this 2-spinor (with σ_z derivable from σ_x σ_y up to phase).

**The R3 question:** Is there an SL(2,7) subgroup H such that H acts on σ₄ via a homomorphism H → SU(2) (or H/Z(H) → SU(2)/Z(SU(2)) = SO(3)), making the Cℓ(0,2) generators identified above into the Pauli σ_x, σ_y (and σ_z derived)?

Equivalently, in formal terms: is there a subgroup H ⊆ SL(2,7) with a 2-dimensional faithful complex irrep ρ such that σ₄|_H ≅ ρ ⊕ ρ' (with ρ, ρ' two copies of the same SU(2)-like rep, possibly twisted)?

#### Why this is an exploration target rather than a conjecture

The structural setup is suggestive but the identification is not yet matched:

- **What matches:** σ₄ harbors Cℓ(0,2) ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ natively (V4.7 R1). The Pauli/quaternion algebra ℍ⊗ℂ is the algebra of SU(2)'s fundamental representation. The 168 anticommuting pairs from order-4 SL(2,7) elements provide an abundance of Pauli-σ-pair candidates.

- **What does not yet match:** An SU(2) subgroup of SL(2,7) acting compatibly on σ₄ has not been exhibited. SL(2,7) is finite (order 336); SU(2) is a continuous Lie group. Any "SU(2) action" must be a FINITE subgroup of SU(2) (a binary polyhedral group: cyclic, binary dihedral, binary tetrahedral 2T = SL(2,3), binary octahedral 2O, binary icosahedral 2I) acting on σ₄ such that its image in σ₄'s 4D space is concentrated in a 2D faithful subrep over ℂ. SL(2,3) ⊂ SL(2,7) is the natural candidate to test first — it has order 24 = (8)(3) and would furnish a binary-tetrahedral action.

#### The three sub-questions

A formal answer to the R3 target requires three layers of work, each load-bearing:

**QQ-1: Subgroup identification.** Does SL(2,7) contain a subgroup H isomorphic to a binary polyhedral group (cyclic ℤ_n, binary dihedral BD_n, binary tetrahedral 2T = SL(2,3), binary octahedral 2O, or binary icosahedral 2I = SL(2,5)) that acts on σ₄ in a way carrying the Cℓ(0,2) structure?

Concretely: identify H ⊆ SL(2,7) and a decomposition σ₄|_H = ρ ⊕ ρ' where ρ, ρ' are 2-dim H-irreps. The natural first candidates are:
  - The subgroup ⟨x, y⟩ generated by an anticommuting pair of order-4 elements; this is the "quaternion group" Q_8 if x, y, xy all have order 4 with appropriate relations.
  - SL(2,3) ⊂ SL(2,7), which has order 24 and a faithful 2D complex irrep (the binary tetrahedral group's fundamental).

**QQ-2: Pauli-matrix identification.** Once H is identified, exhibit explicit isomorphism Cℓ(0,2)_σ₄ ≅ Pauli algebra, with the order-4 Γ_x, Γ_y becoming σ_x, σ_y (and σ_z = ±iσ_xσ_y derived). This is a basis-change calculation given QQ-1.

**QQ-3: Physical mapping.** If QQ-1 and QQ-2 succeed, can the framework's quaternionic 1-spinor be identified with a physical SU(2)-spinor such that:
- The per-vortex carrier mentioned in Path B of the ferromagnetism conjecture is exactly the SU(2)-doublet of the identified subgroup H.
- Shell-level packing across the 2ℓ+1 orientation slots produces observable magnetic moments via the standard non-relativistic exchange-interaction mechanism, with the framework supplying the algebraic substrate but not the dynamics.
- Or, if not, what other physical interpretation the quaternionic 1-spinor carries.

#### Promotion gate to R2

Promotion of any part of §2.E-QQ to R2 requires **at minimum** an explicit construction satisfying QQ-1 and QQ-2 (with the identified H and the Pauli-matrix isomorphism written out as 4×4 matrices in the σ₄ basis). QQ-3 is downstream; it cannot be addressed without QQ-1 and QQ-2 first.

A negative result on QQ-1 (no compatible binary polyhedral subgroup exists) is also a legitimate closure of §2.E-QQ. The exploration is genuinely open in both directions.

#### Standing constraints on this exploration

- **§2.D-FC compliance.** §2.D-FC remains in force: K₇'s spin double cover SL(2,7) does NOT have a 2D faithful complex irrep. The SU(2) action sought in QQ-1 is therefore necessarily a SUBGROUP action, not a quotient or factor action. The 2D faithful irrep lives on a strict subgroup H, not on SL(2,7) itself.

- **§2.45-OPM Finding 1 compliance.** Any work under §2.E-QQ must not cross the per-vortex / shell-filling scale boundary without an explicit bridge (per the lesson logged in the V4.6 ferromagnetism conjecture update and re-iterated in §2.E-WD's V4.7 closure).

- **Quaternionic chirality vs SU(2) spin.** Cℓ(0,2) ≅ ℍ⊗ℂ as an algebra is structurally the Pauli algebra; this is established. But identifying the σ₄-image of an SL(2,7) subgroup with the SU(2) FUNDAMENTAL representation requires showing that the GROUP STRUCTURE matches (not just the algebra structure). A finite subgroup H ⊆ SL(2,7) has the Pauli algebra acting on it via the σ₄ embedding; whether H itself is a binary polyhedral group inside SU(2) is the load-bearing identification.

- **Galois-twist preservation.** The F₂₁ Galois-twist of §2.77 Part IV relates σ₄ ↔ σ₄' as Galois-twisted irreps. Any SU(2)-like structure identified on σ₄ should be tested for whether the F₂₁ Galois-twist preserves it, exchanges it with a Galois-twisted SU(2) on σ₄', or breaks it. The relationship between the Galois-twist and any SU(2) action is itself an interesting open question.

#### Connection to the ferromagnetism conjecture (Path B re-opened concretely)

Path B of `unaudited_conjecture_incomplete_closure_ferromagnetism.md` (V4.6 status note) had stipulated "F₂₁ is not the right structure for ferromagnetism, and a different per-vortex property must be identified that *does* admit a 2-component representation." V4.6 §2.D-FC closed this off the SL(2,7) full-group representation theory (no 2D faithful irrep). V4.7 §2.E-QQ reopens it via the more nuanced route: the 2-component representation may exist on a SUBGROUP of SL(2,7), with σ₄ decomposing under that subgroup into two copies of a 2D faithful rep. This is the new R3 substrate for Path B.

If QQ-1 closes positively (a binary polyhedral H ⊆ SL(2,7) acts on σ₄ via H → SU(2)), the per-vortex carrier proposed by Path B has a concrete algebraic anchor. If QQ-1 closes negatively, Path B remains structurally unsupported.

#### What is NOT being claimed by opening this target

Opening §2.E-QQ as an R3 exploration target does NOT commit the framework to an SU(2)-spin-doublet picture for K₇. It is logging the question of whether such a picture is structurally available *as a subgroup phenomenon* (rather than as a full-group phenomenon, which §2.D-FC has already closed). Both positive and negative answers are held open until QQ-1 is settled by explicit construction.

#### Open follow-ups raised

- **OP-2.E-QQ.QQ1:** Identify all binary-polyhedral subgroups of SL(2,7) (cyclic order 8, binary dihedral, SL(2,3) = 2T, etc.). For each, compute σ₄|_H and check for a 2 ⊕ 2 decomposition. Standard finite-subgroup-of-PSL(2,7) classification (Dickson) applies upstream.
- **OP-2.E-QQ.QQ2:** For each H from OP-2.E-QQ.QQ1 that gives 2 ⊕ 2, exhibit the Pauli isomorphism explicitly.
- **OP-2.E-QQ.QQ3:** Map the per-vortex carrier of Path B to the identified H-doublet, with care to bridge the per-vortex / shell-filling scale per §2.45-OPM Finding 1.
